Fellow Patriot - Today is it.

Like Lindsey, I grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. My parents worked every single day to make ends meet. There was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in.

clean_body: Election Day is today. Help me reach every voter — and fuel the fight still ahead — before midnight. | Fellow Patriot - Today is it. The Primary Special Election for the United States Senate seat here in South Carolina, I'm not a politician. I never expected to be running for office, and I never wanted to. I'm doing this because I'm answering President Trump's call to serve, and because I believe South Carolina deserves a fighter in the Senate. Like Lindsey, I grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. My parents worked every single day to make ends meet. There was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in. That's the kind of work ethic I've carried my whole life, from running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget to turning it into a national model for helping people find work and live independently. I'm a mother, a grandmother, and a wife. I support the Right to Life. I believe in showing ID to vote. I oppose DEI. I stand for the national anthem, I believe our veterans are heroes, and I will always Back the Blue. President Trump wants a fighter in the Senate - that's why he's in my corner in this race, and why I'm asking you to be in it with me. Here's what I need from you right now, in the final hours before the polls close: If you live in South Carolina, make sure you vote today, and don't stop there. Call your friends, your family, your neighbors, your coworkers. Make sure they have a plan to get to the polls before midnight. Every vote we don't turn out tonight is a vote we can't get back. Every dollar raised today will help us build the momentum we need not only to win today but also to win in November. And I need to be honest with you: winning tonight is only the first step. After this Primary Special Election, we still have a long road ahead to the General Election, and this fight doesn't end when the polls close. I will need you again. But it starts with tonight. Help me finish strong. Thank you, Darline Graham P.S. I am the first woman United States senator in South Carolina history. Folks,
Just one week into the general election, we’ve been enjoying a daily barrage of good news, while John McGuire keeps stepping in it.
Since we clinched the nomination, I’ve been barnstorming the district, arm and arm with former candidate Dr. K, who I consider a dear friend. McGuire, on the other hand, is busy being torched by his primary opponent, Melanie Lucero, for being a “puppet” and “disappointment.”
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/perriello-em?amount=50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/perriello-em?amount=50]
Speaking of things my opponent is setting on fire: money.
McGuire blew $1.6 million to boost his primary race, and left himself cash-strapped. Now he’s begging the dark money corporate groups for more cash. And working families throughout the district have caught on to who McGuire really works for.
My campaign couldn’t be more different. Thanks to YOUR incredible, fired-up support, we’ve got the momentum. We’ve got a grassroots army that’s already knocking doors and spreading the good news – that we are going to reclaim Congress for the people!
Since you made me your nominee, I’ve been to every corner of the district. Mecklenburg and Lunenburg to Goochland and Louisa, Fluvanna and Buckingham to Danville to Lynchburg, and back to Charlottesville and Albemarle – and that’s just this week ! We’re not leaving a single stone unturned or a single voter un-talked to. We’re building a coalition of Democrats, Independents, and fed-up Republicans ready to restore our communities and our Constitution from the lunacy and corruption coming out of Washington.
And every single town I stop in, every single door I knock, stoop I sit on, diner I eat in, I hear the same thing: we’re ready to win, together.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/perriello-em?amount=50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/perriello-em?amount=50]
We have been out in the community, helping to distribute book bags to kids headed back to school. Seeing our communities rally, even as McGuire has made everything more expensive for parents, keeps me going.
All of this is to say: we’ve got the momentum, and McGuire’s got a mess on his hands.
If you want to keep this going, consider making a grassroots contribution (or another, if you’ve already generously donated!) to build up my campaign for the general. We know MAGA is ready to pour millions of dollars into this race to protect their puppet and Trump’s rubber stamp, so we need to be prepared to counter their attacks with strong pushes of our own. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/perriello-em?amount=50]
Thank you so much for being on this team and for every single thing you’ve done so far to help get us here. Together we will out-work, out-organize, and out-vote, and together we will win!
—Tom

Mecklenburg and Lunenburg to Goochland and Louisa, Fluvanna and Buckingham to Danville to Lynchburg, and back to Charlottesville and Albemarle – and that’s just this week ! We’re not leaving a single stone unturned or a single voter un-talked to. We’re building a coalition of Democrats, Independents, and fed-up Republicans ready to restore our communities and our Constitution from the lunacy and corruption coming out of Washington. And every single town I stop in, every single door I knock, stoop I sit on, diner I eat in, I hear the same thing: we’re ready to win, together. [] We have been out in the community, helping to distribute book bags to kids headed back to school. Seeing our communities rally, even as McGuire has made everything more expensive for parents, keeps me going. All of this is to say: we’ve got the momentum, and McGuire’s got a mess on his hands. If you want to keep this going, consider making a grassroots contribution (or another, if you’ve already generously donated!) to build up my campaign for the general. We know MAGA is ready to pour millions of dollars into this race to protect their puppet and Trump’s rubber stamp, so we need to be prepared to counter their attacks with strong pushes of our own. [] Thank you so much for being on this team and for every single thing you’ve done so far to help get us here. name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: My generation is starting to be decisive at the polls.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
When pundits do the “Monday Quarterbacking” and look at what demographics voted where in this insurgent wave, the generational tidal wave is often ignored.
Millennials are not punk kids anymore. We’re grown adults with mortgages and kids. My generation is starting to be decisive at the polls.
And there is real anger at having been ignored, sidelined, having our economic futures mortgaged by the generations that came before us — on everything from the economy to climate.
We’re taking the reins. And we know that we don't have to live like this anymore.

Friend, I need to be clear about what’s at stake in this election: **Medicaid. SNAP. Universal Childcare.**
**My Republican opponent has proposed cuts to all three.**
He’s taking his cues from Donald Trump, who has already made thousands of New Mexicans hungrier, sicker, and poorer. **_My opponent isn’t going to stop Donald Trump from cutting the very programs we need._**
**[_That’s why I need your help, friend. A new poll shows my Republican opponent 6 points ahead, and we cannot afford to take this election for granted. I’m running to protect Medicaid, SNAP, and Universal Childcare — programs that help New Mexico families afford healthcare, put food on the table, and give their kids a strong start. But I can’t win this race without you. Will you chip in $5 today to help me close the gap and protect these essential programs?_](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15614?refcode=jtk1198-fr-nd&amount=5&t=2&akid=11667%2E400544%2E4jW7Gn)**

Friend, I’ve relied on Medicaid, SNAP, and WIC. I know what it’s like to work hard, stretch every dollar, and depend on these programs to make sure your family has what they need.
_My Republican opponent clearly doesn't._
Nearly half of New Mexicans rely on Medicaid. We have the highest SNAP participation rate of any state in the country. And since Universal Childcare was rolled out, more than 40,000 families have enrolled.
These programs make sure New Mexican families can get the healthcare they need, put healthy food on the table, and get the support they need to care for their children and go to work.
**These programs aren’t just worth protecting. They’re worth fighting for. Our families deserve the chance not just to get by, but to thrive.**
That’s why, alongside protecting Medicaid, SNAP, and Universal Childcare, I’ll fight to give New Mexicans a raise, make it easier for farmers and ranchers to sell their goods here at home, expand Universal Childcare, and strengthen our healthcare system by recruiting more nurses and doctors and making it more accessible to all New Mexicans, and so much more.
**I will never stop fighting to give New Mexicans the opportunity to get ahead and thrive.[_But if we’re going to meet this moment, we need the resources to win. So please, will you chip in $5 or whatever you can spare today to help me win this race, stop these cuts, and protect the programs New Mexico families rely on?_](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15614?refcode=jtk1198-fr-nd&t=7&akid=11667%2E400544%2E4jW7Gn)**

These programs make sure New Mexican families can get the healthcare they need, put healthy food on the table, and get the support they need to care for their children and go to work. These programs aren’t just worth protecting. They’re worth fighting for. Our families deserve the chance not just to get by, but to thrive. That’s why, alongside protecting Medicaid, SNAP, and Universal Childcare, I’ll fight to give New Mexicans a raise, make it easier for farmers and ranchers to sell their goods here at home, expand Universal Childcare, and strengthen our healthcare system by recruiting more nurses and doctors and making it more accessible to all New Mexicans, and so much more. I will never stop fighting to give New Mexicans the opportunity to get ahead and thrive. | | Be fierce, Deb | | | | | |

The federal government spent $1.5 billion of your tax dollars to buy two ICE detention center facilities that it was already using, including Otay Mesa Detention Center right here in San Diego County.
https://timesofsandiego.com/immigration/2026/07/20/federal-government-purchase-otay-mesa-detention/ [https://timesofsandiego.com/immigration/2026/07/20/federal-government-purchase-otay-mesa-detention/]
The other facility is California City Detention Center, the largest ICE detention center in our state. Both were owned by CoreCivic, a private company, and as part of that deal, DHS purchased Otay Mesa for $739 million — even though it was recently valued at just $168 million. (And yes, Donald Trump owns stock in CoreCivic, but his blatant corruption is a whole other conversation.)
For now, CoreCivic is still running the facilities day to day, and we have a lot of unanswered questions about what this deal actually means. I’m deeply concerned it’s an attempt to ramp up local immigration detention, prevent Congressional oversight, and shield the government’s actions from public scrutiny and accountability.
But let me be super clear: changing the deed of who owns this detention center doesn’t change the obligation to treat every single person humanely, and respect their legal, civil, and human rights.
I’ve inspected Otay Mesa numerous times, both announced and unannounced.
At a recent visit, I raised concerns about medical, legal, and language access issues directly with ICE and CoreCivic representatives, pushing for answers on behalf of everyone in our community who has reached out and shared what they’ve seen and heard. I’m grateful to all the folks who’ve been calling and emailing my office — thank you!
I’m going to continue showing up and asking hard questions. Not just because conducting oversight is my job, but because our community deserves transparency, accountability, and dignity. ICE promised answers to my questions and concerns, and I’m going to hold them to it.
Our community deserves to know what is being done in our name. Because I don’t believe what this administration is doing is making us safer. In fact, it’s making us less safe.
Most of the people held at Otay Mesa are there because of civil violations, NOT violent crimes — but they were often violently detained by ICE agents in riot gear while at work, or arrested when they showed up at their immigration court hearings.
I’m not going to let a change in ownership at these horrific detention centers become an excuse to shut Congress out.
So while I keep pushing back, I ask that you keep it up, too. Keep showing up for your neighbors and speaking out against injustices — that’s how we make a difference right now.
– Sara

body:

A few months ago, my husband and I lost a pregnancy.
The physical toll was something not even my doctor prepared me for.
After 11 weeks of hope about bringing a new member into our family, we learned the pregnancy was no longer viable. After several weeks of bleeding and mourning, my doctor made clear that future pregnancy could be much more difficult if I didn't take medication to expel the retained miscarriage.
Like most women, I was told the medication would feel like a regular period. Maybe a little stronger cramping.
But when I took the medication, the pain was more intense than the pain I experienced delivering my son four years ago. I wasn't even advised to take it when my son was out of the house.
And I am not alone.
Women are routinely told that Ibuprofen is sufficient pain management during miscarriage. In practice, that's the functional equivalent of handing someone a stick to chew on.
Science and medicine have advanced in so many ways, but when it comes to reproductive health, the standard of care for women's pain in this country is still medieval.
I know there are broad differences in beliefs about reproductive health. But we do not need to agree on every policy question to agree that women should not have to endure excruciating pain while managing a miscarriage and protecting their ability to go on and bring a child into this world.
One in four women will likely experience a miscarriage. We can do better than telling them to take Ibuprofen and endure it.
That's why I introduced and passed a simple amendment directing the NIH to study strategies to improve pain management during miscarriage.

clean_body: ? [?] A few months ago, my husband and I lost a pregnancy. The physical toll was something not even my doctor prepared me for. After 11 weeks of hope about bringing a new member into our family, we learned the pregnancy was no longer viable. After several weeks of bleeding and mourning, my doctor made clear that future pregnancy could be much more difficult if I didn't take medication to expel the retained miscarriage. Like most women, I was told the medication would feel like a regular period. Maybe a little stronger cramping. But when I took the medication, the pain was more intense than the pain I experienced delivering my son four years ago. I wasn't even advised to take it when my son was out of the house. And I am not alone. Women are routinely told that Ibuprofen is sufficient pain management during miscarriage. In practice, that's the functional equivalent of handing someone a stick to chew on. Science and medicine have advanced in so many ways, but when it comes to reproductive health, the standard of care for women's pain in this country is still medieval. I know there are broad differences in beliefs about reproductive health. But we do not need to agree on every policy question to agree that women should not have to endure excruciating pain while managing a miscarriage and protecting their ability to go on and bring a child into this world. One in four women will likely experience a miscarriage. We can do better than telling them to take Ibuprofen and endure it. That's why I introduced and passed a simple amendment directing the NIH to study strategies to improve pain management during miscarriage. If you agree that women deserve better pain care than the status quo provides and that the Senate should pass this amendment, add your name today. [] ADD YOUR NAME [] We don't need to agree on everything to agree on this: Women who lose a pregnancy deserve compassion and dignity. ### The accelerating global climate catastrophe should be driving decisions at the local, national, and international level--yet neither elected leaders, nor journalists, nor even voters seem to care

Apologists for the status quo, including the president, have long argued that climate change is a "hoax." Events unfolding around the world should convincingly disprove them, but even as related calamities [continue](https://substack.com/redirect/01840d65-6abd-4813-8772-86685326846a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to destroy lives and [communities](https://substack.com/redirect/3320c73d-f2da-4c83-b785-1c0de5c49998?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), America's corporate political parties continue to drag humanity towards a meteorological abyss with limitless risks to human life & health.
### **A whole way worse than the sum of its parts**
At the same time that Asia is confronting [catastrophic flooding](https://substack.com/redirect/f33a592f-1c41-4bda-a5f7-18e8837aee88?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) driven by typhoons strengthened by global climate patterns, others--particularly the Pacific Northwest and western [Europe](https://substack.com/redirect/41bbf726-0bcf-4ba1-9200-712e3bca3d90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--are battling [unprecedented wildfires](https://substack.com/redirect/767d7fe0-cc03-4956-b8b2-26af565e4749?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

Either of these patterns would be bad enough. China has evacuated over a million people fleeing floods inundating major cities including Shanghai, while wildfires burning near Madrid and Paris have prompted alarm and anxiety across Europe.
The juxtaposition, however, suggests a whole far worse than the sum of its parts.
International agencies and non-profit organizations have spared no alarm. The United Nations Environment Programme, for instance, has noted that "The world may soon cross some potentially disastrous tipping points," and powerfully depicted the scale of climate chaos through [data visualizations](https://substack.com/redirect/af1b9c18-073a-4f0c-9719-7a28f7d2aedc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Yet, while these globally interlinked unfolding disasters have attracted worldwide attention and concern, the pattern that connects them continues to be effectively ignored by elected leaders and journalists across the United States.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8c4d747d-5a0f-4bc8-84d8-c2ff20aa50b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

### **A war making everything worse**
The war in Iran is offensive for many reasons. The [sheer imbecility](https://substack.com/redirect/55335f39-0b1a-46f3-ac67-219b62f966e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that enabled it will be remembered by whatever vestiges of human civilization survive the next generation.
Its damage to the global economy continues to mount by the day.
But the relationship between war and the acceleration of climate chaos is, in fact, the dumbest thing about the whole sordid endeavor. Ultimately, the Pentagon is the Earth's [leading institutional consumer ](https://substack.com/redirect/d34f7135-9827-43ca-bf90-3383b22e3105?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)of fossil fuels, while its actions--particularly in the Middle East over the past six months--have made fossil fuels more scarce, and less secure to extract or ship.
Beyond this long applicable global analysis of the Pentagon's carbon footprint, Trump's war on Iran has also sparked an acute [global fertilizer shortage](https://substack.com/redirect/839dfdcd-3bb1-4db2-adef-a37d8c31a58c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over the past six months, which has already done incalculable damage to crop yields and the global food supply.

### **Don 't look up**
Severe weather events are an indication of climate change, but are not themselves the underlying problem. Like the election of the president, they are severely problematic examples of dysfunction driven by systems besieged by long festering crises: corruption & money in politics helped enable the president, while a series of interrelated feedback loops have consistently accelerated climate change over the past generation.
Looking beyond the planetary symptoms to consider the underlying pathology leads to a further set of challenges that few in positions of institutional leadership have adequately considered.
Many stories, published by any number of news sources, have explored the unfolding El Nino in the South Pacific. Some have even considered its disturbing implications. Few, however, have placed it within the broader context of the climate crisis, considering it not only as a driver of predictable weather calamities, but as a reflection of shifting ocean currents that themselves hold massive implications for the longer term future.
Oscillations in the world's oceans are responsible for much of the movement that carries water and heat across them. Yet two of the most significant: the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) in the North Atlantic, and the Antarctica Circumpolar Current (ACC) near Antarctica, appear to be weakening due in large part to climate chaos.
As Dr. Morgan Sinclair recently [observed](https://substack.com/redirect/5f903c4e-390c-4f6a-8548-3e509f873bd1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on this platform:
> Together these currents run a global "conveyor belt" of ocean water that both cools and warms the planet--releasing excess heat near the Arctic Circle while simultaneously warding off the next ice age by keeping the world warm enough that it doesn't freeze.
> Worldwide, north and south, the circulation of the seas is slowing down. That's trouble.
Dr. Sinclair goes on to explain in some detail how the AMOC and the ACC function, and why they matter so much.
Put simply, melting polar ice reduces the salinity of ocean water, which traditionally grew as water near the poles froze into ice. As the polar salinity pump diminishes, so does the force with which cold, salty water descends to the bottom of the ocean.
Scientists have long warned of the severe consequences of the ocean currents stalling. Hollywood directors have dramatized those consequences (for instance, in _The Day After Tomorrow_ , and _Waterworld_). Millions of young people around the world, driven by their awareness of preventable crisis, have taken to the streets to voice their demands for faster and more meaningful climate action.
Yet Washington stumbles in circles, while the AMOC and ACC continue to weaken, threatening crops & food supplies around the world.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1018597&post_id=210844550&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjEwODQ0NTUwLCJpYXQiOjE3ODY1MDM4NzQsImV4cCI6MTc4OTA5NTg3NCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTEwMTg1OTciLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.RIDrbVjVOwmWozztEChSe-PTmHaoyKmD1RYeYBc_a-8)
### **Strap in**
Despite all the mounting attention to it, the El Niño brewing in the South Pacific will likely prove more destructive than anyone can possibly describe, only because its effects will cascade long beyond the season is over.
Mark Roberts recently [explained](https://open.substack.com/pub/markroberts995/p/scorched-harvest-the-strongest-el?r=97w99&utm_medium=ios) that:
> An El Niño is not a storm. It does not arrive with wind and fury and then recede. It is a reorganization of where rain falls on Earth, a slow, hemisphere-spanning transfer of moisture away from the croplands of Southeast Asia, southern Africa, Central America, and northeastern Brazil, and toward places that cannot use the rain to produce food such as the open Pacific, the deserts of coastal Peru, the flood plains of the Horn of Africa. _**The warm water is only the mechanism; the failed harvests are what people will actually live through.**_ Since the global food system runs on a handful of staple crops grown in a handful of climate-exposed regions, a sufficiently large _**El Ni ño is not a weather anomaly at all. It is going to be a global food shock on a twelve-month fuse.**_
This should be the lead story in every news publication on Earth. It should remain on the front page every day until elected leaders who have ignored this long-festering crisis are finally replaced.
To its credit, _the Guardian_ at least publishes opinion articles about the crisis. Today, Peter Gleich [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/9dc5583e-d234-45f1-98fa-a071cbc23a71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> At any given moment, there are always places around the world suffering from droughts or floods or experiencing water scarcity - a normal consequence of the natural variability of our climate and weather.
> But what we're experiencing now is not normal; it is the direct consequence of accelerating human-caused climate changes, on top of decades of neglect and underinvestment in our water institutions and infrastructure.
> For years, climate scientists have warned that continued emissions of greenhouse gases from burning fossil fuels and other human activities would alter the planet's climate, raise temperatures, disrupt weather patterns and worsen extreme events, raise sea levels, and accelerate the spread of disease vectors. Those warnings were ignored, dismissed, downplayed. And now we are reaping what we've sown.
> Yet our politicians continue to prevaricate, refusing to take actions to protect water resources; or worse, rolling back earlier efforts.
Every day, journalists cover some aspect of the accelerating global climate catastrophe. Yet, even as eyes around the world turn towards some portion of the climate disaster forcing future generations into misery, the phenomenon as a whole--and its disturbing implications--seems to escape polite conversations, especially among policymakers.
Apologists for corporate rule within the Democratic party, for instance, [imagine](https://substack.com/redirect/b20a177a-5254-4787-a9dc-5a3a4a3ab168?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that climate is a divisive issue that is electorally inconvenient. But there is no more important issue to discuss.
The urgency of decisions that should have been made 20 years ago to protect the future grow increasingly insufficient as our leaders continue to bury their hands in the sand, and double down on a fossil fuel paradigm that threatens life on Earth.
> [| | | Shahid Buttar 1dHow are neither politicians, nor journalists, nor even voters, willing to consider the inescapable reality that should be driving their most urgent decisions?
> ---
> https://substack.com/@adammckay177538/note/c-311279990
> | 27| | 10|
> ---|---|---|---](https://substack.com/profile/15484941-shahid-buttar/note/c-312109637)
On the one hand, many institutions have grappled with the implications of climate chaos. The British insurance industry, for instance, conducted an analysis that predicted [4 billion deaths](https://open.substack.com/pub/rogerhallam/p/the-insurance-industry-predicts-mass?r=97w99&utm_medium=ios)--amounting to literally half of humanity--in the next century.
Meanwhile, major news outlets fawn over the president's [vanities](https://substack.com/@reedgalen/note/c-310251813?r=97w99&utm_medium=ios&utm_source=notes-share-action) rather than issues that will dramatically affect (or even end the lives of) billions of people.
### **Hands in the air**
I'll be honest: I have no idea how to overcome these patterns.
After dedicating years to direct action organizing, and more than half a decade to promoting better policies as a candidate for Congress, I learned the hard way that our system does not permit meaningful change. I've watched journalists and voters decide to preserve documented corruption at the cost of their own grandchildren's survival.
As far as I can tell, America's elected leaders, and the journalists who create cults of personality surrounding them, are oblivious. So, too, are voters who continue to send the same corporate shills back to Washington as if they hadn't engineered a preventable calamity that makes every other unfortunate event in human history look like a blessing by comparison.
As a writer and former candidate for public office, I've tried my best to [offer hope](https://substack.com/redirect/a9052d99-b998-4f53-8cfe-231087e87073?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to people concerned about the future. But [trying to conjure hope for young people](https://open.substack.com/pub/climatecasino/p/an-unexpected-message-from-the-edge?r=97w99&utm_medium=ios), in particular, has grown painfully futile. Many are more aware of the future crises that corrupt elected leaders have contrived than those leaders themselves.
I've been relatively publicly silent lately. But that's not because I can't find issues to write about.
Sadly, every day offers new horrors that have led me to start dozens of half-drafted articles. The problem constraining me is that, as a writer, I have always offered my ideas with an eye towards a broader process. My aims have included informing people, inspiring them, and building grassroots social movements to force our shared concerns into political institutions.
But America's corruption makes that process appear like a cruel joke. I wish I could offer you hope. But I have a hard time lying.
That said, I can at least share a little information, and a few ideas that could still make a difference.
### **None of this is rocket science**
Faced with catastrophic risks to life on Earth, a sane civilization might consider alternatives that would lead to greater sustainability.
Capitalism, however, is not sane. Capital is rapacious, even to the point of destroying the people who wield it.
Given the relationship between the Pentagon and climate chaos, the very first thing we might do to address the climate catastrophe would be to stop investing in its expansion. Reducing the military budget is a long overdue no-brainer.
Shifting some of those resources recovered from the military budget to climate resilience would make even more sense. Among the many possibilities that come to mind--such as organizing [controlled burns](https://substack.com/redirect/312620f8-f72f-49e2-8842-c1c4026ab8a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during the winter season to reduce the propensity of severe fires in the summer and fall, municipal [composting systems](https://substack.com/redirect/abbf271c-cf4e-4533-a182-7e328c311fb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to reduce waste and reuse bio-resources, and a youth jobs corp dedicated to cultivating local permaculture & sustainability projects--few seem as pressing as simply paying firefighters what they're worth.
Across the country, firefighters are currently confronting the leading edge of the climate crisis. Like military servicemembers, they spend weeks or months on the road, facing severe risks to their life and health while away from their families.
Many work without adequate support from local, state, or federal governments. Some are forced to [buy their own equipment](https://substack.com/redirect/0a83d4a2-57aa-408a-b638-c0e8c181da92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
On the one hand, federal firefighters received [a long overdue raise](https://substack.com/redirect/aeded907-d24c-4f9a-821d-0c3d567d1f69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last year. On the other hand, a [recruiting crisis](https://substack.com/redirect/2af2ffa3-383e-4d65-8cb8-9d20dc7e0350?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) continues across the country, suggesting that resources currently funding weapons, or military recruitment--or local policing, for that matter--could find better uses.
Finally, nationalizing the fossil fuel industry is a crucial step in removing the powerful incentive of corporate profit from the scale. I've argued before that allowing the extraction of non-renewable resources for profit forces the future to subsidize the present. It is a recipe for civilizational self-destruction.
Nationalizing the sector--by allowing extraction only by public agencies that do not pursue profit--should have happened decades ago. Of course, any other country that has attempted to pursue that path has faced a [CIA coup in retaliation](https://substack.com/redirect/e48823c1-9aa5-4c73-bbab-09b7a1e829e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), so I have little hope that Washington will permit that policy to see the light of day in the U.S.
But the future of life on Earth increasingly depends on it. As long as capital is allowed to profit from fossil fuel extraction, human beings will all remain reduced to its fodder.

The accelerating global climate catastrophe should be driving decisions at the local, national, and international level--yet neither elected leaders, nor journalists, nor even voters seem to care | | | Aug 11 | | | | | | | | | | | | Apologists for the status quo, including the president, have long argued that climate change is a "hoax." Events unfolding around the world should convincingly disprove them, but even as related calamities to destroy lives and , America's corporate political parties continue to drag humanity towards a meteorological abyss with limitless risks to human life & health. A whole way worse than the sum of its parts At the same time that Asia is confronting driven by typhoons strengthened by global climate patterns, others--particularly the Pacific Northwest and western battling . Thanks for reading Chronicles of a Dying Empire! If you learn anything from this post, please share it. Either of these patterns would be bad enough. China has evacuated over a million people fleeing floods inundating major cities including Shanghai, while wildfires burning near Madrid and Paris have prompted alarm and anxiety across Europe. The juxtaposition, however, suggests a whole far worse than the sum of its parts. International agencies and non-profit organizations have spared no alarm. The United Nations Environment Programme, for instance, has noted that "The world may soon cross some potentially disastrous tipping points," and powerfully depicted the scale of climate chaos through . Yet, while these globally interlinked unfolding disasters have attracted worldwide attention and concern, the pattern that connects them continues to be effectively ignored by elected leaders and journalists across the United States. | | ---|---|--- Cartoon by A war making everything worse The war in Iran is offensive for many reasons. The that enabled it will be remembered by whatever vestiges of human civilization survive the next generation. Its damage to the global economy continues to mount by the day. But the relationship between war and the acceleration of climate chaos is, in fact, the dumbest thing about the whole sordid endeavor. Ultimately, the Pentagon is the Earth's fossil fuels, while its actions--particularly in the Middle East over the past six months--have made fossil fuels more scarce, and less secure to extract or ship. Beyond this long applicable global analysis of the Pentagon's carbon footprint, Trump's war on Iran has also sparked an acute over the past six months, which has already done incalculable damage to crop yields and the global food supply. To support my work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber. Don 't look up Severe weather events are an indication of climate change, but are not themselves the underlying problem. Like the election of the president, they are severely problematic examples of dysfunction driven by systems besieged by long festering crises: corruption & money in politics helped enable the president, while a series of interrelated feedback loops have consistently accelerated climate change over the past generation. Looking beyond the planetary symptoms to consider the underlying pathology leads to a further set of challenges that few in positions of institutional leadership have adequately considered. Many stories, published by any number of news sources, have explored the unfolding El Nino in the South Pacific. Some have even considered its disturbing implications. Few, however, have placed it within the broader context of the climate crisis, considering it not only as a driver of predictable weather calamities, but as a reflection of shifting ocean currents that themselves hold massive implications for the longer term future. Oscillations in the world's oceans are responsible for much of the movement that carries water and heat across them. Yet two of the most significant: the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) in the North Atlantic, and the Antarctica Circumpolar Current (ACC) near Antarctica, appear to be weakening due in large part to climate chaos. As Dr. Morgan Sinclair recently on this platform: Together these currents run a global "conveyor belt" of ocean water that both cools and warms the planet--releasing excess heat near the Arctic Circle while simultaneously warding off the next ice age by keeping the world warm enough that it doesn't freeze. Worldwide, north and south, the circulation of the seas is slowing down. That's trouble. Dr. Sinclair goes on to explain in some detail how the AMOC and the ACC function, and why they matter so much. Put simply, melting polar ice reduces the salinity of ocean water, which traditionally grew as water near the poles froze into ice. As the polar salinity pump diminishes, so does the force with which cold, salty water descends to the bottom of the ocean. Scientists have long warned of the severe consequences of the ocean currents stalling. Hollywood directors have dramatized those consequences (for instance, in The Day After Tomorrow , and Waterworld). Millions of young people around the world, driven by their awareness of preventable crisis, have taken to the streets to voice their demands for faster and more meaningful climate action. Yet Washington stumbles in circles, while the AMOC and ACC continue to weaken, threatening crops & food supplies around the world. Strap in Despite all the mounting attention to it, the El Niño brewing in the South Pacific will likely prove more destructive than anyone can possibly describe, only because its effects will cascade long beyond the season is over. Mark Roberts recently that: An El Niño is not a storm. It does not arrive with wind and fury and then recede. It is a reorganization of where rain falls on Earth, a slow, hemisphere-spanning transfer of moisture away from the croplands of Southeast Asia, southern Africa, Central America, and northeastern Brazil, and toward places that cannot use the rain to produce food such as the open Pacific, the deserts of coastal Peru, the flood plains of the Horn of Africa. The warm water is only the mechanism; the failed harvests are what people will actually live through. Since the global food system runs on a handful of staple crops grown in a handful of climate-exposed regions, a sufficiently large El Ni ño is not a weather anomaly at all. It is going to be a global food shock on a twelve-month fuse. This should be the lead story in every news publication on Earth. It should remain on the front page every day until elected leaders who have ignored this long-festering crisis are finally replaced. To its credit, the Guardian at least publishes opinion articles about the crisis. Today, Peter Gleich : At any given moment, there are always places around the world suffering from droughts or floods or experiencing water scarcity - a normal consequence of the natural variability of our climate and weather. But what we're experiencing now is not normal; it is the direct consequence of accelerating human-caused climate changes, on top of decades of neglect and underinvestment in our water institutions and infrastructure. For years, climate scientists have warned that continued emissions of greenhouse gases from burning fossil fuels and other human activities would alter the planet's climate, raise temperatures, disrupt weather patterns and worsen extreme events, raise sea levels, and accelerate the spread of disease vectors. Those warnings were ignored, dismissed, downplayed. And now we are reaping what we've sown. Yet our politicians continue to prevaricate, refusing to take actions to protect water resources; or worse, rolling back earlier efforts. Every day, journalists cover some aspect of the accelerating global climate catastrophe. Yet, even as eyes around the world turn towards some portion of the climate disaster forcing future generations into misery, the phenomenon as a whole--and its disturbing implications--seems to escape polite conversations, especially among policymakers. Apologists for corporate rule within the Democratic party, for instance, that climate is a divisive issue that is electorally inconvenient. But there is no more important issue to discuss. The urgency of decisions that should have been made 20 years ago to protect the future grow increasingly insufficient as our leaders continue to bury their hands in the sand, and double down on a fossil fuel paradigm that threatens life on Earth. On the one hand, many institutions have grappled with the implications of climate chaos. The British insurance industry, for instance, conducted an analysis that predicted to literally half of humanity--in the next century. Meanwhile, major news outlets fawn over the president's rather than issues that will dramatically affect (or even end the lives of) billions of people. Hands in the air I'll be honest: I have no idea how to overcome these patterns. After dedicating years to direct action organizing, and more than half a decade to promoting better policies as a candidate for Congress, I learned the hard way that our system does not permit meaningful change. I've watched journalists and voters decide to preserve documented corruption at the cost of their own grandchildren's survival. As far as I can tell, America's elected leaders, and the journalists who create cults of personality surrounding them, are oblivious. So, too, are voters who continue to send the same corporate shills back to Washington as if they hadn't engineered a preventable calamity that makes every other unfortunate event in human history look like a blessing by comparison. As a writer and former candidate for public office, I've tried my best to to people concerned about the future. But , in particular, has grown painfully futile. Many are more aware of the future crises that corrupt elected leaders have contrived than those leaders themselves. I've been relatively publicly silent lately. But that's not because I can't find issues to write about. Sadly, every day offers new horrors that have led me to start dozens of half-drafted articles. The problem constraining me is that, as a writer, I have always offered my ideas with an eye towards a broader process. My aims have included informing people, inspiring them, and building grassroots social movements to force our shared concerns into political institutions. But America's corruption makes that process appear like a cruel joke. I wish I could offer you hope. But I have a hard time lying. That said, I can at least share a little information, and a few ideas that could still make a difference. None of this is rocket science Faced with catastrophic risks to life on Earth, a sane civilization might consider alternatives that would lead to greater sustainability. Capitalism, however, is not sane. Capital is rapacious, even to the point of destroying the people who wield it. Given the relationship between the Pentagon and climate chaos, the very first thing we might do to address the climate catastrophe would be to stop investing in its expansion. Reducing the military budget is a long overdue no-brainer. Shifting some of those resources recovered from the military budget to climate resilience would make even more sense. Among the many possibilities that come to mind--such as organizing during the winter season to reduce the propensity of severe fires in the summer and fall, municipal to reduce waste and reuse bio-resources, and a youth jobs corp dedicated to cultivating local permaculture & sustainability projects--few seem as pressing as simply paying firefighters what they're worth. Across the country, firefighters are currently confronting the leading edge of the climate crisis. Like military servicemembers, they spend weeks or months on the road, facing severe risks to their life and health while away from their families. Many work without adequate support from local, state, or federal governments. Some are forced to . On the one hand, federal firefighters received last year. On the other hand, a continues across the country, suggesting that resources currently funding weapons, or military recruitment--or local policing, for that matter--could find better uses. Finally, nationalizing the fossil fuel industry is a crucial step in removing the powerful incentive of corporate profit from the scale. I've argued before that allowing the extraction of non-renewable resources for profit forces the future to subsidize the present. It is a recipe for civilizational self-destruction. Nationalizing the sector--by allowing extraction only by public agencies that do not pursue profit--should have happened decades ago. Of course, any other country that has attempted to pursue that path has faced a , so I have little hope that Washington will permit that policy to see the light of day in the U.S. But the future of life on Earth increasingly depends on it. As long as capital is allowed to profit from fossil fuel extraction, human beings will all remain reduced to its fodder. body:
In seismic new development, Mike Johnson announces he will back an avowed Neo-Nazi. The move signals an extreme new turn to the extreme far-right for the Republican Party.
| | | | | [](https://jseax8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001bLBScF5iE112CxcjzoiSWEZzWLjCxuQ9UDo_qv7WGpjLIeIIjUajpXcKTbeN2ITgmlUa2WrpE_JoRoOfX83_jHIchOMMP4nUZtAi38_ORB8ZUZ7-1tWsZCiRaCT0O10BczpT-2lflh0FQK--Uf99aCgGDDCj3JX7VWOonwgioGDs2i8Xf4evga5Wl-REzC_scS1kDGOZ1oV0QwGlGOJyL3B_NDk3cUx7&c=YgKVj2VHFURfHHy00xrfYtQO1x_8igIpXn2eB76Wqc9VjU8kRggf3Q==&ch=y4zyndVi_vtE4UmjpPSiMnhLByb65oscPhNdLYiulnNhKZYx7uP4_Q==)
---
Peter,
A disturbing turn of events has led to an avowed Neo-Nazi earning the nomination for a must-win GOP race, Texas's 23rd Congressional District.
In April, MAGA's first choice, Congressman Anthony Gonzales (R-TX), resigned following a disturbing sex scandal in-which a staffer whom he was having an affair with tragically committed suicide on his front lawn by lighting herself on fire.
At the time of his departure, Gonzales was being primaried by Neo-Nazi Brandon Herrera. With no serious opponents Herrera was the last man standing and is now the nominee for TX-23.
Today, in a seismic new development, Speaker Johnson announced he will be backing Herrera at the hilt signaling an extreme new turn to the extreme far-right for the Republican Party.
---
| [](https://jseax8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001bLBScF5iE112CxcjzoiSWEZzWLjCxuQ9UDo_qv7WGpjLIeIIjUajpXcKTbeN2ITgmlUa2WrpE_JoRoOfX83_jHIchOMMP4nUZtAi38_ORB8ZUZ7-1tWsZCiRaCT0O10BczpT-2lflh0FQK--Uf99aCgGDDCj3JX7VWOonwgioGDs2i8Xf4evga5Wl-REzC_scS1kDGOZ1oV0QwGlGOJyL5EKDG0_WpE4&c=YgKVj2VHFURfHHy00xrfYtQO1x_8igIpXn2eB76Wqc9VjU8kRggf3Q==&ch=y4zyndVi_vtE4UmjpPSiMnhLByb65oscPhNdLYiulnNhKZYx7uP4_Q==)
---
| Herrera, 2nd in line, dressed in a WW2 era German SS Paratrooper Uniform carrying a German MG-42 performing a Nazi goosestep march.
---
Herrera made a name for himself as a gun Youtuber and in his videos he has cosplayed as a Nazi-Paratrooper, flaunted his 1939 edition of Mein Kampf, and made crude sexual jokes about the mothers of school shooting victims.
In one video on his channel, he recreated the MLK assassination, reviewed the alleged shooter's rifle, and shot an MLK target dummy at close range.
Herrera prides himself on his neo-Confederate credentials as a member of the Sons of Confederate Vets. Refers to the Civil War as the War of Northern Aggression, and advertises an annual Yankee shoot, where he and fellow neo-confederates shoot at "posters of their favorite Yankees."
My name is Conrad Cable. I'm the Democrat taking on Speaker Mike Johnson, the head of the hydra, who is working to restore Confederate monuments and ensure that people like Herrera make it into the House where they can legislate their views into reality.
My family has been in Louisiana since 1824 and I can proudly say not a single one of us fought on the side of the Confederacy. I am in this fight because I refuse to let Johnson and his ilk have their way and lead our nation into another conflagration.
Speaker Johnson's fascist push must be stopped at all costs and I am the only one who can stop him.[ ](https://jseax8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001bLBScF5iE112CxcjzoiSWEZzWLjCxuQ9UDo_qv7WGpjLIeIIjUajpY3oPm8D4j9c0lx1sNxyaBFHAxe_ZmNhu5gWP7XzHHtvaFoUe6avztJdjlkFvsVBLA5nYKssgYFX&c=YgKVj2VHFURfHHy00xrfYtQO1x_8igIpXn2eB76Wqc9VjU8kRggf3Q==&ch=y4zyndVi_vtE4UmjpPSiMnhLByb65oscPhNdLYiulnNhKZYx7uP4_Q==)[This is the fight of my life and I need your support to rapidly scale this campaign. The “Working People Party” is deliberately confusing and deceiving working class Nebraska voters to support MAGA billionaire U.S. Senator Pete Ricketts.
| | | | | [](https://eeuwd7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001sbUHDYD7sFapuqRY5mb4_HUtM1y7EAxaUmi0PPaxuB15ISxXOggBHguJIqzbMMpOJAZbtPmNbZ_EoxaJJaAxbG34yFxAL6ChKNXzcqfrSJJWehLNShaoU7YJPwzYr3M5M5if8TmG-vR1lxDTlfO_mnTZq4bWfLXOPnhHePz2pnOOOR9l77emfN7xRsCZDK77SMguahKYwRQmUyyDyfHR6z7EiQYXE0cI&c=2veNdRX_zfeqPWADmDqggk91r4fnymcyDLO2mXCetuIaW1Ks7bkH5w==&ch=KFj6xp8RSmMXgOoeWkGwRS9VHn8-X_jMhRV0_iJyKz_1TADEEHmKEg==)

Peter,
We're back in court. Nebraska Democrats are taking decisive action to stop a fake political party led by a sore-loser former candidate from tricking voters this midterm.
The so-called "Working People Party" is deliberately confusing and deceiving working class Nebraska voters. They are actually supported by MAGA donors all to help Senator Pete Ricketts.
Our lawsuit exposes how this brand new party was intentionally designed to mislead voters in two ways: first, by mimicking the Working Families Party's name -- in likely violation of Nebraska law -- and secondly, by echoing the "working people deserve a seat at the table" message central to independent U.S. Senate candidate Dan Osborn's campaign.
But we aren't just making legal arguments--we're revealing the right wing plot to cheat and deceive Nebraska voters in court:
An out-of-state conservative paid operative was caught red-handed on video trying to convince prospective petition signers to support getting WPP on the ballot by saying "if you're a Republican, [WPP] is very liberal, it's going to take votes away from the Democrats."
---

---
The right wing operatives pushing this phony party label have no business appearing on November's ballot.
Unfortunately, dirty tricks like this are par for the course with MAGA.
That's why we're fighting to protect Nebraska voters and make sure their choices this November are crystal clear: we can elect leaders with integrity up and down the ballot who will hold Trump and MAGA accountable; or we can keep the same corrupt people in office who are leading our country down a dangerous path and screwing working people every single day.
Waging these critical fights on so many fronts puts us at risk of depleting all of the resources we need to turn out every last anti-MAGA voter in November.
Flipping two House seats and defeating Pete Ricketts is going to come down to turnout--and we will fall short if we don't make up for it right now.

| Friend,
---
| **The last few weeks have been terrifying for Democracy.**
---
| Trump went on primetime to resurrect his election-fraud fantasy, laying the groundwork to contest any result he doesn't like. Stephen Miller stood at the State Department and called Americans on the left a "cancer" to be "rooted out." The FBI raided the Ohio Organizing Collaborative and opened an investigation into America Votes, two groups whose only crime is registering voters.
---
| _And, Trump’s reign of terror continues._ On Monday, the State Department published a report titled "Cuba: The Capital of 21st Century Communism." Buried inside it is something that has no business existing in a free country:**a list of specific American citizens, named and targeted by their own government for their politics.**
---
| [](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001fGHI0MIQZC8rpjwzUZsKaZsGlzI682nyxoRw8UGwx2VeaLHbenjdT3k6sA6WsjdFMd6hpEIvNZMvK9bAU-o2JRgV3V9khk_Z1c_qcIKO96h8XO1iIA5d-N4kOl_bynHaQgBxjs8GjBATY4uejOE8PACdhlgPZXu6DMOxpM_o4iKT8pF5oB868p4rgfRqS_jsZYzDi51RgTB61P04q-QKwHXFD9yX-QiE7tgFsWwapJJPcNarHiQaHZXH3-0_s-qGSyKiC6-mRcU=&c=KFSCbKk1Rn17nbMJ-uT8mR7ryR3sQ08oQJq8H5aCCLw1fbsAN0UoLg==&ch=lxC2N4KdcyuhzwBRmXfhKshA2K6JXqTRSD-VJtlrUBHAtCGjQ9Xhcw==)
---
| _**A pattern is starting to emerge.**_
---
| The report singles out streamer Hasan Piker, Amazon union organizer Christian Smalls, the Democratic Socialists of America, and environmental activist Isra Hirsi, the daughter of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar. It brands them "front groups and fellow travelers" for a foreign government, and it reaches back to the McCarthy era for its playbook, holding up the blacklists and loyalty purges of the 1950s as a model _that worked._
---
| _You don't have to agree with one word these people have ever said to see the danger._ The instant the government starts printing lists of citizens to punish for their beliefs, _**the only question left is will my name get added next.**_
---
| And just as terrifying, this report serves another insidious purpose: it lays the groundwork for regime change in Cuba as Trump continues to threaten an invasion. _A witch hunt at home and another war abroad._
---
| **That’s why Defend Our Courts’ work is so critical at this moment.** Trump’s attempt at a fascist takeover of our country is exactly what our courts were built to stop. The judges we elect this November will play a decisive role in whether our democracy holds or not. We’re fighting to expand and protect the Democratic firewall of state Supreme Courts nationwide— _courts that have the power to stop Trump._
---
| **But to operate at the scale we need to at this pivotal moment requires resources we don’t have yet. We need the support of Democrats everywhere to help fuel our efforts.**_**That’s why we’re asking today:**_****[Can we count on you to rush a donation of $25, $15, or whatever you can spare to help us fight back against Trump’s fascist takeover?](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001fGHI0MIQZC8rpjwzUZsKaZsGlzI682nyxoRw8UGwx2VeaLHbenjdT3k6sA6WsjdFhWpE3JfcF1g8ULXQb4Z7cO3iPQD-Ue8lQ3TlxiujOJx2F4NwZzL6veVGH72v0QUJl1-9mqap9imZuoGH8d5h7DVgJPXvXpjSlSWGqRrW-EPHmNhci9HfTPMfvvKe7v2Iu9uyaNZY939A_QCS7teaKxd9ykQwg875Gn4Srdh7wrUXYkm8aoO1jf0HOE4-rcOxVuAB9Til6bw=&c=KFSCbKk1Rn17nbMJ-uT8mR7ryR3sQ08oQJq8H5aCCLw1fbsAN0UoLg==&ch=lxC2N4KdcyuhzwBRmXfhKshA2K6JXqTRSD-VJtlrUBHAtCGjQ9Xhcw==)

## Report Reveals Trump's Security Ruse
President Trump [secretly switched planes](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O2zAQBOCnoToa5FoUdQWLNOoubUqBIVfHDfgjkGsbfvvABlKkvnoXg_nm1-f-6SlT_frpCzo-2l7xMTIyY9-538o5MNw68fPM7Tla9h1D3kHBItUqNew-MN1xn_0U3YEIeJ3QabsuBj7Amim5iCauGGA-8IpaLcZ8xBkXDb9tsMbGidwrT60atFLWzJdoVqVUsEsIEYPSYlYYiVu__GlUOeGRn-2O_RJambJLzOcQ1x8CNgEbJ0yU8-smYEut4IskYPOxUKXB3TO1KmBbFGhrtYyt-hzlmyv_eWVoNWCvQ3rq8mg9oGwV5Zl9RTkexCHJ6rnJcSuFWHKiHv9_FrBN3cXzQTnTWKyY1Vfx9O428Tfnvjv4GwAA__-XjZls) while leaving last month's NATO summit in Turkey, an elaborate ruse detailed in new reporting this week. The president and several aides were [driven across the tarmac](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O3DoMhuGrkTsOJI7_tnBxGnd72pSGItFjZmXJoOhZ-O4D7y2kJvECz_frc_n0nDi__vc7TbqWJdN3TaRKsqic-1EpnMJ6HalctSQvFNKCFnuwIzhcfFB-09L6Jk4rEdKzockNY9_hBw5ds00fgxvR0dr9jj7EGNH2T9cPrvX4DGTXhqe7Z0eHztqhax-xG621YehDiBSsM62lyFrk8adw1o3WdJU3ySOUvUnTpnpU8_zP4GxwztdRqt4ng_MdNjjb0eDsrMH5rHALDc4_Oqj5DF9Q1hU8C6xFAkHJBJwheCXh_AKV-yfS4UUpgp7yRReUDJWCkMLOidXLBWvi16bgd47A4jPoJuQVhI4ianBuZIrHN6fEtR9Ma1-75_Sj0H8c_z3h3wAAAP__WUuc9Q) in a catering truck to the plane's far door, then boarded a smaller, lookalike military jet.

Journalists and White House staffers aboard _Air Force One_ had no idea their plane flew home as a decoy. Watch [how the President pulled off the switch here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ8GOtDiYIMLF39Dl7-9EjnrJeydwchsgnj7E3mF6z5ppNF883Uf754jr8__fiEnUxpXOvZIIpRHya9l2wlfmeXcYjr3FH0mjKMCZSroq0aNHoXfNLa-DG4iUnQryTVdb7SyqtPl7KChdgqBbnoios7TQwM9rFEajbXWluyuPugb1QB0uq2D7gEAO4MYCKEpWqDAknL9nXiVmaZ4pjflGtNSRjeLbHtx-1eooVDDcRz16eeUrrRQwyVUqGFLkYXxQp-FMdKFH8Vq5hBordALZV6fleQX_lQ7YSapwIIBbZu-nmWJZXZhOzhG3k1XtPBcPMfPDvnjfW-nfgMAAP__ikWHWA). The operation came after U.S. intelligence detected a credible Iranian threat to [fire a missile](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uhDAQhJ_GdEaL-TEpXKShu7Qpkc9eDicGo_XeWbx9xL1CupFGGs33fd_mmw0x7I8vu6HhJc07lhyRGWlmem5HRvekwOcR05lTtIQuzgrUIGGUjZqt4_DCubOVNwuiwrZC0-hx6NWH0n21mmGAoXXaewX92C6wQA_6rq1tulbbrqmCufZgbFQDoPuu9v0IAE4Pznl00IgO0AdOVP-ksPOKSzzTC6l2aauiWZmPLNpPoSahplJK7e754rh6oaYrCjW9cWRGR8jxlLkEdit6eUS7o-Qn_eIpbSC5JHIo044ykN1lsSR5JbQs1FSR8UcJMYY8aNHBY7Mhvn_wP_W9jPoLAAD___VMh84) at the presidential plane, officials told media, one day after American strikes on Iran resumed.
## Bipartisan Backlash Hits Flock Cameras
A nationwide backlash against Flock Safety's license plate cameras is [becoming bipartisan](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkc2qnEAQhZ-m3dXQtr934WJCEBK42WSRpZRlOVamtaWrHfHtw9xXyO7AgQPf-f58Dp8oXrbHL1y5S3MYNj7Vc0ochxSPdVemI0q6dh8uDR4jkx-cdTXYFnI3ICV58VBiNnUzs-Mi4y5v2rpyH66psqXjap7LprDNiEhTNVJVtejqD0aa2orrTLr3nm1zl1vbVOVtqlprLTU10cRkc1NaniSFePsbZEsLz_4KL443CmvmuyWlXU1xN643rj_P87bq9u6M63mDQ43r31jG9V_5DPEJYwhJAbcJ9BgxHgo-EHoI8ywk6BUUL0gLw4j09KgL4ANl0wSzD_QEwpUjKojCyBRW2R4wyo4xieJmXI8R7nf38ePndZqiDySTKb5_e3_Np_7muGexm_ZTvBetG1Pax4riv5jSf6p4de5fAAAA__88gqNV), local officials say. More than 20 communities cut ties with the surveillance company in July alone, the most in any month on record. The solar-powered cameras photograph every passing vehicle and log 20 billion plates a month, and Flock says they played a role in about [1 million investigations](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2unDAURldjOiP7goEpXIwi0U3alOjGvoAT_yDbDGH30bwtvPb7pKOj8-u1vNB5F7efGEjXNS2RruKpVspLzWc4Cpkzu3ofPt0lecxk_AICBi4mLmFBU92blh4bq1cioK4hLcdpUPCAUTW7ViRl33WrAGXtCP2qxgnVA_r1MZmJ1sbpD09MEqQQo-pbqyYhhBkHYywZIVkvyLqacvsnuVh3Wv2d3pRbk0Lj9V7rUVj3ZDAzmK_rakOJn4_BTJGfhcEcUqSbwWxSODA6-mx1Jx6xuhQvZ4n_RvPXY9k5buhiqdxgoIyFX1jN7uLG73RmbjAzmDHz5xOGH_-EbLK2x-W8d2UYWS-2gM5_qdVvFn1r-B8AAP__swuNUw) last year. But conservatives see government overreach, liberals see tracking of immigrants and protesters, and both are showing up at city halls to fight the cameras. Frustration has [boiled over into vandalism](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1u9CAQQE-DO1sw6x9cUHwN3X5tSouF8S4JGAtmbfn2EZFygjRTjd57Mx_35W588Nvzv4moaE3LhmcJSIR5ofyOe0H7zp6uPaSrpGAy2rAAh7HlshWwGEv-wKU3jVMrIuCtQSUmOQ4wwzQ0LyUkykE--snxGfEhV2lWACvXW-8eYp4aryqPSwGC82noOzdIzrmdRmsdWi5Yz9F5Srn7TH6jF67hSgfmzqbYBPUi2gu7_WOgGejzPLt3MZScueoCA10o5YuBrrcx0Db7iAx0tTLQXP6ONST71VoTMZv2MJszwZfY2rRRrr5SIbMQcz_MNZWBbrJy--lD8GWcWM-f0fjw00V_fOeh4DsAAP__w4WJEQ). Cameras have been shot, sawed down, beaten with a baseball bat, and splattered with paint, and more than 20,000 people have registered for a national week of protests later this month. Lawsuits arguing the tracking violates the Fourth Amendment are moving through courts in several states, and Republican lawmakers have proposed barring federal funding for the technology.
## Robocalls Reach Highest Level in a Year
Robocalls are [spiking nationwide](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO3CAQhJ_G7jgtGBv_BUUad3_alBYHa7PJ2iDg7uS3j5xXSDkzmtHo-_W9fjtiOvef7kDbtrSe-KmMrWFZW3kduaJ_FWpX5nTVxK6g51WBmgTMQqrV-UZvXLXrg90QFQ49WmnmaVRfyox9tPPwFQLAc5u1ktoZM5gA4-gGqZ0GJ3uy9x7MUkkAM-pHGGcA8GbyPqAH2WnAQC2Vx-9EZ4u48ZXeWB4-HT3b2Fqu3fCjU0unlhYxEvOddWrJiclft40-nonTfosJFJhZipKeyTvmKlxBUTP9oXMXWDN6csyX2FIROaYTxfk6nliq-FCLokWseHec8Clg7dTSFxvyh5ipTqbTsB-O_p3o239yfVv1NwAA__--uY-l), with Americans fielding more spam calls in July than in any month in the past year, according to call-screening service YouMail. The tally topped [4.3 billion calls](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkb2upDAMhZ8GOqMQws8UFNtMd7fdEmUcz5CrkCDHGZa3XzHFvsAtLft81qfz52v5sj74-PptN5rlmZZIRw4kQrwIl23PhIW9nHtIZ07BMmFYtNIDqAlavVgU_6bF2NrNTyJNXU1zO05Dr2967Ot1to8OO31rezWNQ-uG3uBDmf52I3wiDar288VTU6tbpcbeNK6flFI4DoiOULWVUeS8JG6-k4-y0jOc6U3cYNrqMK8ie666X5W-V_p-HEez86VxeKbrpNL3awSmQDZTrvS9ZOD0SGhDyIApio-FoOyHZQfCFB3YzyKXjfiKIvk3OdgSE8hqIxjo4OFD8CmCj_BdwgkWMbHz8QWS4Exlsz78fwQ-OvoLndKTMeNkmlW2UPPs9uPC5GGsjHpdkY-X_LCO96z_BQAA___tSqU6) in a single month, and the most common was a fake "pre-approved" loan offer promising big money at low payments. YouMail calls it illegal telemarketing at scale and likely a scam. Numbers with Houston's 346 area code saw the sharpest jump, up 19% in one month, followed by codes covering Atlanta and Albany in Georgia, and much of Indiana and Tennessee. But no region was spared. A bill cracking down on overseas robocalls recently passed the Senate. Until then, experts say: Don't pick up. Let unknown numbers go to voicemail, and always call your bank back on the number printed on your card, not the one that called you.

# Wednesday, August 12, 2026

**Good Morning!** On this day in 1862, Union gunboats blockading the Texas coast [opened fire on Confederate forces](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGu2yAUgOGnwVsswBjsgaGN5C1dOyICh_io2FhwEqdvf5X7Cnf8l2_4_97czWPG_fHHb2DpnYrb4WwZiKC6WMsObX3u1EKF8yx1u5caoTrJpb7w6SKk84HwBU75Lto7j7PowAoz6XGQSstutSmF4HUclAlzGs0dopqCN3IMXvA4qg7th-OTkEJwPs69NjHNoLSeBmV8VExxiEil9rQCwdu3lP-XF9Q-lK3LdiU6Ght-MbkwucDen_gPD4jo-1IfTC6fZnL57YkyuJLctdTj2dx1rdgIu2rjcWLO2LRhij82j_nbpp8-eVn5FQAA__-m7Hk5) in Corpus Christi Bay. The shelling of the port town went on for a week. You'll see a bunch of three-digit numbers in our _Weather_ section today, but our top _Et Cetera_ item links to a list of the coldest Augusts in Texas history. Do you remember the summer of '71 or 2004? Let us know in the _Poll_ whether you'd prefer a cool August or a warmer January. Do you think you're a good driver? A new study asked nearly 2,700 drivers about the risky things they do behind the wheel, and the answers reveal a strange gap between what people believe and how they actually drive. Here's one that will sting. It's something 61% of us do in the car, barely anyone considers it dangerous, and research shows it can scramble your focus for nearly half a minute after you stop. And the kicker: 78% of drivers believe they're safer than everyone else on the road, and researchers say that belief is wrong and dangerous. So, which of the top 5 knowing mistakes are you guilty of? Today, Ayla counts down the driving errors we all talk ourselves into. [Tune in here](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykz7FugzAQgOGngS3IPhtjBg9dsqVrR2S4I1gyODpfQ_L2VfsKfYD_l76v23SLKafj_hl3CvJay3TQWTOJEE_I5aC6fR9SF6bzLLzPhZF4AgXuovxFwxQXSU-abGwxzApH3VLQg3e9Aeug3QLS2mvsjZp9RD-qVfe4wgwzLMYba9oUfnfKa9BaqX7s3IDrSNY5b-wQ0TZWESYp3MlGQq9Y1_wuT-JuKXubwybyqI35aODawJVp5nhgl98NXB8F6SUcdcsBH2fKOVU3NFbd95jyXy__dT8D_AQAAP__U0FuCA)! Today's sponsor is [Blood Sugar Secrets](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0MHOoyAUBeCnwZ0NXBRxwWKSibvOdpYG5KJMUJoL1fbtJ-0r_MuTfDknOX_v893GFI_1j93R1FfI84FXSVgr0uwpH1i251HLQnhdmXaXySPNwEG1XLcCZrvUeOLc2cYbx_0oGjRi0KqX0CloNgOLc2Ec9DiMQfT94L2SvpeopfZuDK6J5lPHtQAhOO_Hmxp8GLFTSstusL5jHUcfa6Zb3bDiy5aQ3vlEui15b5LZan0UJn8xmBhMIVN5rpYIC9aPYDCVldqzJNEm-CA52RDm6Jn8LbRSDFR5um_8t2sBIb1dXFekhox_XDGlWNTAOr7uNqbvaP3pWaeB_wEAAP__Cqd-3w), sharing information about a surprising factor that may offer clues about blood sugar health and a simple approach being discussed for supporting healthier blood sugar levels.

## Texas School Vaccine Rules Unchanged
Texas students need the same vaccines this school year, despite President Trump's [executive order on](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpCAUhZ9GOwwiA1pQbGM3225pGO51JAExcJWZt9_4v8Jfnpzk5Hzfv-fytD74_f3XRjT0WdOyYy0BiTAvkNOOZTt3Ki5jrSnHV8qAeRFcKMZH1ovFOvIXLtK2YF4cpr5F0-tRPQYhlWg3YyenpxdosPjAEbkYrRqUnITSenXKtd7cc3zsRd9z_pg6pWGdUCo1DlJbkI3kCJ5S7mhDwo8ta_imC3PnUmyD2YiO0gx_GjE3Yq61dmv63Bx334j5SMGTd6URs9t8AHZZ5_yOrLgN4QzIMsLpEBjlMx4spgsLg2yjJe9sCF9WNr8Siwh3ZkeqmNlhM-5U2mzgqD4EX5RuJH9H68PPM_qt0cuI_wEAAP__C8eQ5g) Monday trimming federal childhood vaccine recommendations. The order [cuts universal recommendations](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2y2yAQBeCnQR0eWMlIKlSkobtpU2owLIYJPw6srJu3z8ivkH5nz_nOr6_9y8QUy_OnybjRt697wbMnJMK2u1YL9nAU6rbhedaWH7U5bDsIUFwsXMJuLMU37pMZ3PYQbpUDbnJe1H2EScEQNiG9Fw788vB-9qgU4t2aeVzGdV4n4Ye4Xe_EIkFKIe7rTc3OrzgptYzTbNzEJoEuUm03Ckj4bbpPf-sb283WPKQtEL06G38w0Az0eZ43m6L9DaEenWq5rhjoC8ZAp2pNYqCvTAZaLAy0lAw0tSO_-MfHbTDliZ3bEJMLtTr-NtbGgryhrTljcYZiLZ0_DuKfSrzbUGviDf8csWHGQp03zCYWHgt_JWORgR7a5l5nTCl2NbNJPLOJ6eOg_93_vcG_AAAA__82bp6s) from 18 diseases to 11 and calls for splitting the measles, mumps, and rubella shot into three separate doses. Trump said parents can still choose every shot, and that [insurance will cover them](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSpSAQRb8GMyxoFTUg2IRsNt3Q4kEzUoViQavz_n7L9wuTddB9-p7772v5sjHF_fuv3VDTT8jLjndNSIRl8SXvWNdzp-oK3ncu2ysXj2UBAYqLiUtYrKN44dLbxuuX8LNsUMtxUkMHvYJm1R0EsJ30g-vcEJxDJWaPY5gcBC_mron6wYlJgpRCDHOrRh9m7JWaun60vme9QB8pl5ZWJPyxNaR3vrC0Lm9N0ivRUVn3h4FhYO77bs9qKXv7fhYYmEq5vBmYx42BOXKKFN0zPp8ZGDExMFIwMFTO7eBHsbFi5Zd1Lu7IP9b8dRJ35XPKA9rC3RqT5x4trQ9sljCIYR6EGBmYpmh_3DGlWNXIevG92Zg-iem3TV8a_gcAAP__pOeTUA). The Texas Department of State Health Services called it a guideline, not a mandate, and said nothing changes for the 2026-27 school year. Only the Legislature, which returns in January of next year, can change state requirements. Rebecca Hardy of Texans for Vaccine Choice [praised the order](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAQhp8Gd0QwJtguKK5xt9deaRFmHCNhyA2TZPftT7uvcPUv_d-n78_H9hFzyfX-O54U5HNvW6V3LyRCvCG3Sv14VumJ6f1ufN4aI_EGBrw2s7awxST5RZuLA4abwcUOFOw0--sIzsNwhJloh2kCZ5brdB1hdNbNFuNMNCL425DD952ZLVhrzHW5-An3hZz38-imiE45Q5il8UUOEvqMfS9f7UV8Se0cSjhEHl2NvxSsCtZ4S3b8XhSsXRp_KViR-iML6Z2QOBZN-95YukZuD52OXJCpdv2KKeVKmim186SKUXKrXf8wNdPfZ2Y6qUrXz5qOWO-ECla7eA_OOAXrwAEf71xK7n5SztzPmMuPpvxv3leAfwEAAP__QfSSVg) but wants Texas to broaden exemption rights. Texas still requires hepatitis A and B shots, which the order no longer universally recommends. Last year's measles outbreak killed two children and infected 762 people in Texas.
## Drones Hunt Screwworm on Border
Border Patrol agents launched [heat-sensing drones](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8Gb1j4mWB7YOjiLV07Wtg8YlQMFryG9O-rNFJ_oPPVvTrnflyXq_HBx9u7OVDTw6UlYi0BiTAvNqeIZf-KVLaMtaZ8rClbzAsIUFyMvIPFbOTvuEjTWL0KO3UN6m4Y1aUHqaDZtbtIBHSDNHYcTKfWXkzWbFKszjoYsfH6OSfGDrpOiMvUqsG6CaVSYy8HYyWTAq2nlFvakfBhigvf6Y653dLRBL0TnYX1bwxmBnOttf18mPgMGcwvYp7xTJkYzDsa4gVj8fHGX4Z8x3By56Plf6KFp8hpR_7qM5ibrO1ZfQi-qIFJcTuMD78E9N_n7hp-AgAA__-5i4ca) over Moore Air Base near Edinburg on Monday to scan livestock and wildlife for New World screwworm. An animal carrying the fly's larvae runs a fever, and the drones' [thermal cameras](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwyAUhZ8Gb47ggjEMDF28pWtH69pcx0jYREDs9O2rRGpfoPM5-s7P13W8Yohhv33iRq4-lzTudJZItVIefU47lfWx1zJnOs-UtyllT3kEDrrlphUw4lzDQaPCxruJeysacqI3upOgNDSr66QXs_QWJ6stGE588SAn2Rm0AnFpgnvhuBEgBOedvejeL5aU1kaqHr1iipMPNeVLXanSE8sSv9NB-TKnrYlurfVemPxgMDAY3q1jWOilMhhecAYDNwwGIX4N7d-ktjzyQSFG3Gdq33gGQ5Odv58hxlB0zxS_bRjiO6_-96fDwU8AAAD__2xffWs) detect the spike from the air. Veterinarians then check the animal and quarantine it before the parasite spreads. That's why we need an ironclad line of defense in state governments to stop Trump's takeover of American elections -- starting with battleground Ohio.

name: Jamie (personal)
subject: My grandfather picked cotton on land he'd never own
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jamie Davis for U
body:
And now, I’m carrying his legacy with me each and every single day.
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001USVn0EkqEYOghIa1OchYYe1xKoalhzLJKdmSlGmINFSdqH8tonrUSmy8Oq0lYzLzwWtH_dk_zAr70mQJGPDpl1Y7duZcs--uQMuc-y_6PE0zsyPlQy4yJynJWou2onnsAa6c9PD3zLjEdtGNrtWTKlgCPFpcLlBRvR-W3DNb2an3FRadXoKYR1LMonadppYauWfDLs19T67OI9z3eoOIUYDv5dwkG9-yE-VL--rH8MU=&c=AzkK7hNk5FiI7v4Rc_5rEfOXNliTXmyy1jXI6cteXsjhVo95oknXDA==&ch=hw_g1rM8tpNtuPVVfE_ftBfvVJRLLtaNuS1FRRRa_2yxcLk6cWaPjA==)
---
| Peter,
My grandfather was a sharecropper.
He worked the land from sunup to sundown that he would never own. He picked cotton by hand in the brutal Louisiana heat, breaking his body for a system designed to keep him exactly where he was -- poor, powerless, and dependent on the landowners who controlled everything.
That was life in the Louisiana Delta. My father grew up in that world. In those days in rural Louisiana, many boys left school early because their families needed them in the fields.
Work came first.
But my Dad had a dream that his son wouldn't have to live that way. That somehow, some way, our family would own land instead of working someone else's. That we'd build something that couldn't be taken away.
And he did it. Through decades of backbreaking work, he made that dream real.
We started with 220 acres my father had leased and built it into something real, something ours.
Today, we farm over 3,200 acres. 700 of those acres belong to my family outright.
Some of the same Louisiana delta soil my grandfather worked as a sharecropper -- my family owns it now.
Do you understand how profound that is? How impossible that would have seemed to my grandfather?
And now I'm running to become Louisiana's first Black senator since Reconstruction.
Sometimes I think about what my grandfather would say if he could see this moment. A man living in a system designed to keep him down, whose grandson might represent this entire state in the United States Senate.
It takes my breath away.
This isn't just about me. It's about every Black family in America that was told they'd never amount to anything. Every sharecropper's descendant who was supposed to stay in their place. Every person who was counted out before they even got started.
If I win this seat, it won't erase the centuries of injustice that came before. It won't undo what was done to my grandfather or the millions like him.
But it will prove something powerful: that in Louisiana -- in the Deep South -- we can move forward. That the grandson of a sharecropper can stand as an equal in the halls of power. That our democracy, for all its flaws, can still bend toward justice.
My grandfather never got to see this. My father -- God rest his soul -- never got to see this either.
But my grandkids will. And maybe, just maybe, they'll grow up in a Louisiana where anything truly is possible, regardless of the color of your skin or which side of the tracks you were born on.
That's what this campaign means to me. It's personal in a way I can barely put into words.
And I need your help to make it real.

clean_body: And now, I’m carrying his legacy with me each and every single day. | | | | | == | Peter, My grandfather was a sharecropper. He worked the land from sunup to sundown that he would never own. He picked cotton by hand in the brutal Louisiana heat, breaking his body for a system designed to keep him exactly where he was -- poor, powerless, and dependent on the landowners who controlled everything. That was life in the Louisiana Delta. My father grew up in that world. In those days in rural Louisiana, many boys left school early because their families needed them in the fields. Work came first. But my Dad had a dream that his son wouldn't have to live that way. That somehow, some way, our family would own land instead of working someone else's. That we'd build something that couldn't be taken away. And he did it. Through decades of backbreaking work, he made that dream real. We started with 220 acres my father had leased and built it into something real, something ours. Today, we farm over 3,200 acres. 700 of those acres belong to my family outright. Some of the same Louisiana delta soil my grandfather worked as a sharecropper -- my family owns it now. Do you understand how profound that is? How impossible that would have seemed to my grandfather? And now I'm running to become Louisiana's first Black senator since Reconstruction. Sometimes I think about what my grandfather would say if he could see this moment. A man living in a system designed to keep him down, whose grandson might represent this entire state in the United States Senate. It takes my breath away. This isn't just about me. It's about every Black family in America that was told they'd never amount to anything. Every sharecropper's descendant who was supposed to stay in their place. Every person who was counted out before they even got started. If I win this seat, it won't erase the centuries of injustice that came before. It won't undo what was done to my grandfather or the millions like him. But it will prove something powerful: that in Louisiana -- in the Deep South -- we can move forward. That the grandson of a sharecropper can stand as an equal in the halls of power. That our democracy, for all its flaws, can still bend toward justice. My grandfather never got to see this. My father -- God rest his soul -- never got to see this either. But my grandkids will. And maybe, just maybe, they'll grow up in a Louisiana where anything truly is possible, regardless of the color of your skin or which side of the tracks you were born on. That's what this campaign means to me. It's personal in a way I can barely put into words. And I need your help to make it real. == If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | == | == | == | | | == | == | == | == | My grandfather picked cotton on land he'd never own. subject: Bad news ... good news.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Deluzio for Congress
body:
Today in America, we have more wealth and income inequality than at any time since the 1920s
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=53%2E42639%2E7PJBGd)
Today in America, we have more wealth and income inequality than at any time since the 1920s. We spend more money per person on health care, yet get worse results than just about every advanced country in the world. Families cannot afford to spend time with their newborn children or take care of a loved one when they are sick and need help. And we have a corrupt system of campaign finance where the wealthiest are able to buy elections to keep the status quo in place.
That's the bad news.
But there is good news.
All across the country people are voting for candidates who are saying NO to Donald Trump and a corrupt Republican Party and saying YES to candidates fighting to create a government that works for all of us.
Nationally, the polls agree.
People believe that in the richest country in the history of the planet, we should pass Medicare for All and have guaranteed health insurance for every man, woman, and child in this country.
People believe that having childcare we can afford, paid family leave we can enjoy, and a job where people make a decent wage should not be a luxury in this country.
Now I can already hear the Republican response...
Whenever we talk about spending money to help people in this country, they get religion about "the debt."
Oh no, we can't ensure people have health care ... we gotta bring down the debt.
Oh no, we can't make sure starving children get nutrition assistance ... we gotta bring down the debt.
Oh no, we can't ensure every child has a quality education in this country ... we gotta bring down the debt.
But when it comes time to find $1 trillion in tax handouts for the richest people and corporations in this country, or to fund wars no one wants overseas ... no one is talking about the debt.
**[I recorded a short video on the topic. I hope you'll give it a watch and while you're there like and subscribe to my YouTube channel.](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/373?t=2&akid=53%2E42639%2E7PJBGd)**
[](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/373?t=3&akid=53%2E42639%2E7PJBGd)
Thank you for watching.
Don't give up the ship,
Chris Deluzio

| | **The July CPI Lands This Morning, Expected at 3.4% — Down From 3.5%. But It Will Look Better Than $90 Brent Feels. Here Is the Interpretive Trap to Avoid With Your Portfolio.**
---
| | The July CPI arrives this morning at 8:30 a.m. ET, the most consequential inflation reading of the summer. Economists surveyed by Dow Jones expect 3.4% inflation on an annual basis, down from 3.5% in June, with core CPI expected to rise 0.2% month-over-month and ease to 2.5% year-over-year. **This is the first CPI to carry the full Strait of Hormuz pass-through, and it lands with Brent having touched $90 on Tuesday for the first time this month.** The central question: does energy’s renewed climb overwhelm the modest disinflation economists expect elsewhere?
---
| | For your portfolio, there is a specific interpretive trap to avoid. The July CPI is a backward-looking average: gas prices fell early in July on optimism about the conflict, then rose again as fighting resumed, and on net Bank of America expects gas to show a 2–3% decline in the report. **That is why the headline can ease to 3.4% even as spot oil sits at a monthly high — July’s average was still below June, while this week’s $90 Brent belongs to the August data not reported until September.** For the American investor at or near retirement, a reassuring 3.4% headline this morning should not be read as “inflation is beaten,” but as “inflation eased in July before the August oil surge that has not yet been measured.” The forward energy risk is fully intact and will show up next month.
