There’s not much the hyperpartisan majority on the Supreme Court won’t do for Trump, Peter.
But even the most corrupt Court in the land refuses to budge on overturning the 14th Amendment — no matter how hard Trump pushes them to.
That’s why last week, Trump made another set of unconstitutional executive orders targeting birthright citizenship and so-called “birth tourism.”
Last year, on the first day of his second term, Trump issued a similar order to restrict birthright citizenship. It was struck down by the Supreme Court just a few months later.
His latest executive orders will meet the same fate. But even still, this is the exact kind of rhetoric that puts a target on the backs of immigrant families like mine.
Trump and his MAGA allies have made it clear that regardless of whether you were born in this country or not, if your name is hard to pronounce, if you look different or pray differently, you are not fully American in their eyes. They are using the machinery of the federal government to make that point, loudly and cruelly, every single day.
This is exactly why I started Equal Opportunity Now.
We need leaders in office who will stand up for immigrant families, for the 14th Amendment, and for every community that Trump has decided to make an enemy.
Those leaders exist. They are running for office right now. They need our support.

Don’t believe the spin.

Executives at Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros Discovery want you to think that the lawsuit I filed (along with 11 other states) to block their illegal merger is about politics.

_It’s not._ It’s about the law, plain and simple.

**[This week I wrote a guest column in Deadline laying out the facts of the case, and I hope you’ll read it.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137106796/639662474/1996313446?refcode=260812em_rb_paramount_oped&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTdiZjM3MS02ZDk2LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=v0Uh0yNLWcR1yUtWo7mGXi3x4eYzT0iJkoQhnohvORc=&emci=367bf371-6d96-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=3e7bf371-6d96-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=33430436)**

| | This proposed merger — the biggest in Hollywood history at $110 billion — would create an industry behemoth with an illegal level of concentration in the film and TV distribution markets.

Antitrust laws exist for good reason: if these companies succeed in their scheme to manipulate the market, competition would go down. And if competition goes down, the quality of the content produced goes down, too — along with the number of TV shows and movies produced. _The only thing that goes _up_ is prices._

This is exactly what our lawsuit is working to prevent.

Paramount and Warner Bros see the writing on the wall: they will lose this case in court. So instead, they’re trying to win the court of public opinion by muddying the facts and twisting the narrative.

They are welcome to keep trying — but I will keep fighting our case, and I intend to win.

Thanks for reading and for being a part of this team.

—Rob

Rob Bonta
Attorney General of California

subject: We won! Thank you, Vermont.
body:
Dear Peter, **We won!** I just got back to the office from this morning’s Unity Rally hosted by the Vermont Democratic Party. I stood alongside Democratic candidates from across the entire ballot — Ryan McLaren, Aly Richards, Amanda Janoo, Attorney General Charity Clark, Mike Pieciak, Secretary of State Sarah Copeland Hanzas and Tim Ashe. We came together as one party, ready to storm ahead into the general election in November. I hope you will join me in thanking Esther Charlestin and Ryan McLaren for a hard-fought campaign, for caring deeply about Vermont, and for giving voters a choice. I deeply appreciate Ryan's call last night, support today and I look forward to finding good work to do together with both of these terrific leaders. As the race was called last night, we were surrounded by a small group of family, friends, staff, and volunteers. I am filled with gratitude for you and for every Vermonter who believed in this campaign and helped us get here. **Thank you.** This campaign has been powered by those who believe in this state and are ready to come together to tackle our biggest challenges — from health care and housing to protecting our democracy and fundamental rights. You know, as I do that there are no ceremonial offices, and there is too much at stake. We know Vermont. We know what this office can be. And we know we can win in November. This victory belongs to the incredible statewide coalition we built together: our volunteers and organizers, the Teamsters, the VSEA, Our Revolution, former Governors Madeleine Kunin and Howard Dean, more than 100 Democratic and Progressive elected leaders, and hundreds of Vermonters from Canaan to Pownal and everywhere in between. And most of all, it belongs to **you**. Thank you for sending texts, making calls, putting up lawn signs, talking with your neighbors, making a contribution, hosting a party, sharing our message, and believing in what we can accomplish together. I could not be more proud of the campaign we built. **Now, we get back to work.** I have no doubt national Republicans will pour outside money into Vermont and do everything they can to keep this seat. They will try to divide us. But we will out organize and out work them -- and we will come together, stronger than ever, for this place we are so lucky to call home. To that end,**we're starting from scratch as of today**. **[Will you chip in to refuel our campaign and start the general election campaign off strong?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137106916/639662678/679520187?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1YjIwNzNkMC02ZDk2LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=2F9gZUxlE_JDw1CL4hxrNvyU0W9H40_3iMAhuk8-pPA=)** | If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process now.

clean_body: Dear Peter, We won! I just got back to the office from this morning’s Unity Rally hosted by the Vermont Democratic Party. I stood alongside Democratic candidates from across the entire ballot — Ryan McLaren, Aly Richards, Amanda Janoo, Attorney General Charity Clark, Mike Pieciak, Secretary of State Sarah Copeland Hanzas and Tim Ashe. We came together as one party, ready to storm ahead into the general election in November. I hope you will join me in thanking Esther Charlestin and Ryan McLaren for a hard-fought campaign, for caring deeply about Vermont, and for giving voters a choice. I deeply appreciate Ryan's call last night, support today and I look forward to finding good work to do together with both of these terrific leaders. As the race was called last night, we were surrounded by a small group of family, friends, staff, and volunteers. I am filled with gratitude for you and for every Vermonter who believed in this campaign and helped us get here. Thank you. This campaign has been powered by those who believe in this state and are ready to come together to tackle our biggest challenges — from health care and housing to protecting our democracy and fundamental rights. You know, as I do that there are no ceremonial offices, and there is too much at stake. We know Vermont. We know what this office can be. And we know we can win in November. This victory belongs to the incredible statewide coalition we built together: our volunteers and organizers, the Teamsters, the VSEA, Our Revolution, former Governors Madeleine Kunin and Howard Dean, more than 100 Democratic and Progressive elected leaders, and hundreds of Vermonters from Canaan to Pownal and everywhere in between. And most of all, it belongs to you. Thank you for sending texts, making calls, putting up lawn signs, talking with your neighbors, making a contribution, hosting a party, sharing our message, and believing in what we can accomplish together. I could not be more proud of the campaign we built. Now, we get back to work. I have no doubt national Republicans will pour outside money into Vermont and do everything they can to keep this seat. They will try to divide us. But we will out organize and out work them -- and we will come together, stronger than ever, for this place we are so lucky to call home. body:
Ending unchecked Republican rule starts by electing Roy in North Carolina.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1215&source=&t=1&akid=2673%2E124072%2Eu5R5GH)

Peter,
What we’re seeing out of our nation’s leaders is far more dangerous than politics as usual. Fear is wielded as a weapon. Communities are being targeted. The powerful are pushing boundaries as if they aren’t bound to the same rules as you or me.
**We cannot afford another two years of unchecked Republican rule in Washington DC.**
Whether we’ll have to or not will come down to the Senate race in North Carolina – and if anyone can flip this seat blue for the first time since 2008, it’s Roy Cooper. [**_He’ll need all of us in the fight with him to win, though. Will you chip in today to support his grassroots campaign?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1215&amount=5&t=9&akid=2673%2E124072%2Eu5R5GH)

Serving as Governor alongside Roy was a true masterclass in the integrity and accountability that marks the best of public service. I know I speak for Democratic Governors across the country when I say Roy’s the proven fighter that the people of North Carolina deserve representing them in the U.S. Senate.
Since he’s never lost a statewide race, experts say this is the best shot we have to flip a GOP-held seat this cycle. The GOP knows it too, and they’re spending nearly $100 million so far to end his streak. **If they succeed, they'll likely keep the majority until 2029.**
So we all have a choice to make, Peter: Either we fight to keep our country moving forward or hand over our future to MAGA extremists and their antidemocracy backers. I know which one I choose, and I need you to join me today.

Hey, Last night, voters in Connecticut's first congressional district elected a primary challenger over a long-time incumbent. Former Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin won. Peter,
We did it, y’all.
I am now the official Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota. I’m also proud to have EMILYs List endorse our campaign in this must-win Senate race to take back the Senate majority AND hold Minnesota for Democrats this November.
This community has had my back for years.
EMILYs List stood with me as I ran for lieutenant governor and made history as the first Native American woman elected to statewide office in Minnesota. They were with me when we ran for reelection. And all along the way, they’ve invested in Democratic pro-choice women who are ready to step up, speak out, and lead in every corner of our state.
Now, we’re taking on our biggest fight yet — together.

I got into public service because I believe politics should actually make people’s lives better.
That means making sure every child has a full belly, a safe home, and the opportunity to thrive. It means lowering costs for working families, protecting our air and water, and honoring our responsibility to the generations who will come after us.
And it means trusting people to make their own decisions about their bodies, their families, and their futures. Full stop.
In Minnesota, we’ve shown what can happen when leaders listen to their communities, lead with their values, and aren’t afraid to get things done. **But Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans want to drag us backward.**
They’re attacking abortion rights. They’re targeting our neighbors. They’re giving more power to billionaires while working people are left paying the price. And they want another vote in the Senate so they can keep advancing their cruel, chaotic agenda without anyone standing in their way.
Well, Minnesota has shown the world that we know how to stand up to bullies. _And we’re ready._
This race could determine control of the Senate, so we know exactly what’s coming. Republicans and their billionaire buddies will pour millions of dollars into Minnesota. They’ll distort my record, divide our communities, and do everything they can to distract us from what’s really at stake.
But here’s the thing: We’ve been building toward this fight for years.
EMILYs List has spent decades building a deep, diverse bench of Democratic pro-choice women — in Minnesota and across the country — who know their communities and know how to win. They understand that we don’t build lasting power by parachuting in at the last minute. We build it by finding great candidates early, investing in them, and sticking with them through every tough fight.
We’re ready to defend this Senate seat. We’re ready to protect our freedoms. And we’re ready to show the country what people-powered leadership looks like. Will you have our backs?

clean_body: Now, we’re taking this fight all the way to the U.S. Senate. | = LAUNCHING: STATES IN PLAY 4 days. 4 states. Races up and down the ballot. EMILYs List is supporting Democratic pro-choice women at every level in four of the most consequential states on the map. Today’s state in play: MINNESOTA | = Peter, We did it, y’all. I am now the official Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota. I’m also proud to have EMILYs List endorse our campaign in this must-win Senate race to take back the Senate majority AND hold Minnesota for Democrats this November. This community has had my back for years. EMILYs List stood with me as I ran for lieutenant governor and made history as the first Native American woman elected to statewide office in Minnesota. They were with me when we ran for reelection. And all along the way, they’ve invested in Democratic pro-choice women who are ready to step up, speak out, and lead in every corner of our state. Now, we’re taking on our biggest fight yet — together. = = I got into public service because I believe politics should actually make people’s lives better. That means making sure every child has a full belly, a safe home, and the opportunity to thrive. It means lowering costs for working families, protecting our air and water, and honoring our responsibility to the generations who will come after us. And it means trusting people to make their own decisions about their bodies, their families, and their futures. Full stop. In Minnesota, we’ve shown what can happen when leaders listen to their communities, lead with their values, and aren’t afraid to get things done. But Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans want to drag us backward. They’re attacking abortion rights. They’re targeting our neighbors. They’re giving more power to billionaires while working people are left paying the price. And they want another vote in the Senate so they can keep advancing their cruel, chaotic agenda without anyone standing in their way. Well, Minnesota has shown the world that we know how to stand up to bullies. And we’re ready. This race could determine control of the Senate, so we know exactly what’s coming. Republicans and their billionaire buddies will pour millions of dollars into Minnesota. They’ll distort my record, divide our communities, and do everything they can to distract us from what’s really at stake. But here’s the thing: We’ve been building toward this fight for years. EMILYs List has spent decades building a deep, diverse bench of Democratic pro-choice women — in Minnesota and across the country — who know their communities and know how to win. They understand that we don’t build lasting power by parachuting in at the last minute. We build it by finding great candidates early, investing in them, and sticking with them through every tough fight. We’re ready to defend this Senate seat. We’re ready to protect our freedoms. And we’re ready to show the country what people-powered leadership looks like. _Republicans have lost our polling lead in**Iowa, Michigan, and Ohio** -- all at once._ In Iowa, we had a 0.7-point lead in April. It's now a 0.5-point Democrat advantage. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Israeli settlers continue their raids on the Palestinian village of Taybeh in the occupied West Bank despite the Israeli army declaring the area a 'closed military zone,' on August 10, 2026. Photo by Issam Rimawi/Anadolu via Getty Images.
TAYBEH, Occupied West Bank*--On Sunday, the Israeli military declared the Palestinian village of Taybeh in the occupied West Bank a closed military zone, claiming the order was aimed to prevent escalating attacks by marauding Israeli settlers. It ostensibly bars Israelis and foreigners from entering the area.
But residents of the village and the surrounding area told Drop Site News that the military order is designed to further isolate Taybeh from the outside world, barring solidarity activists from the area while allowing settler attacks to continue. One of the few Christian-majority Palestinian villages in the West Bank, Taybeh has come under growing attacks by Israeli settlers who have expanded colonial outposts encircling it over the past several weeks.
"The order says that Israelis and foreigners are prohibited from entering the area. What about the settler roaming around the area? What is he? Is he Israeli or not? Why is he in the area?," said Jack Abed, the priest of the Greek Catholic Church in Taybeh. "This order is intended to prevent human rights defenders from being present to defend us against what these settler thugs are doing--attacking us in an extremely brutal manner."
The observation was echoed by Nayef Kaabneh, head of the Bedouin community in Taybeh that lives in the lands around the village. "They told us the area had been declared a closed military zone to stop the settlers from coming here. But it turned out that was all lies. The settlers still come here, while the activists are prevented from coming to us," Kaabneh said. "They want to isolate us so they can come after us."
Kaabneh recounted a recent incident when a settler arrived in the area followed by several international solidarity activists. "We called the police and the army. The army came and said, 'This is a closed military zone. Leave.' So the activists left, and the settler left. But the settler just went over there, and once the army left, he came back. And the activists didn't come back. So the order is really aimed at the activists, not the settlers," he said.
On Tuesday, the Israeli military issued a similar decree, [announcing](https://substack.com/redirect/531f49e6-7c38-4113-87fc-13f96d876739?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a military closure on the villages of Kufr Qallil and Jalud, both in the northern Nablus governorate, again claiming it was necessary to protect Palestinian residents from settlers.
Despite occasional statements by Israeli authorities that it does not tolerate attacks by settlers, collaboration by Israeli forces in settler attacks is well established. A UN [report](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf35a5f-fdff-42b0-9d92-c7708c69b872?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory in June concluded that Israeli authorities are directly involved in settler attacks that have killed, injured, and displaced Palestinian communities in the West Bank. "The increasing participation of Israeli security forces in settler attacks amounts to a de facto collapse of the distinction between settlers and soldiers," the report said.
The commission found that "settler violence in the West Bank functions as a means of implementing Israeli State policy, with the State and violent settler groups and individuals working towards the same strategic objectives, including the maintenance of the unlawful occupation, the entrenchment of illegal Israeli settlements, the annexation of Palestinian territory and the displacement of Palestinians from their land." It added, "Israeli authorities have enabled such attacks through financial and military support while Israeli judicial and law enforcement authorities have granted impunity for settler violence for decades."
While attacks by Israeli settlers and soldiers on Palestinians in the West Bank have been a frequent occurrence for years, they have accelerated sharply since October 2023 in parallel with Israel's genocidal assault on Gaza, with over 1,100 Palestinians killed and tens of thousands forcibly displaced.
Last month, the UN warned that attacks by Israeli settlers and the creation of settlements and outposts have hit "an all-time high." Over the past two and a half weeks, the attacks escalated even further following a [raid](https://substack.com/redirect/54069026-928a-4eaa-add3-9658e4283c27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by settlers on the village of Tell that ended with four Palestinians and two settlers being killed. Over the past week alone, there have been over 500 reported attacks, according to the Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission.
Palestinians in the village of Taybeh, which is home to some 1,500 people and lies several kilometers northeast of Jerusalem and Ramallah, said that the settler violence has become all but intolerable. Just over a third of Taybeh--including most of the built up section of the village--is designated as Area B, a classification under the Oslo Accords where the Palestinian Authority is in charge of civil administration while Israel officially retains security control. The rest of Taybeh's lands are designated as Area C, where Israel officially exercises full civil and security control.
"There were attacks before, but nothing like what we're seeing these days," Kaabneh said. "Over the past 15 days, the settlers have been coming two or three times a day, in the morning and in the evening. They've really intensified the pressure on us."
"They want to forcibly displace us," he added. "God willing, we'll remain patient, and God will give us the strength not to leave this place and to remain steadfast here."
Taybeh's churches date back to the Fifth Century. "Taybeh is a Palestinian village, regardless of whether it's Christian or Muslim," Abed, the local priest, said. "The Jewish settler doesn't distinguish--all he sees is a Palestinian."
Israeli settlers have also targeted Taybeh's olive groves, which provide one of the primary sources of income to the village. Multiple residents told Drop Site that settlers bring sheep and other livestock to graze on their lands and use up the water in local wells and also bring camels to chew at the tops of the olive trees and ruin them.
"The camels are destroying the trees because they're such tall, large animals. The tops of the olive trees have been completely destroyed.... These are Roman era olive trees. It's truly heartbreaking," Fouad Maadi, a local resident, said. "Every aspect of life [is affected], everything. Commerce is finished, agriculture is finished, livestock is finished."
"It's a campaign of revenge against us aimed at forcing us out of this land. But we're staying here," he added. "We're not going to leave, no matter what."

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137109984/639673167/2105508926?refcode=ea.65fb9cc2-7296-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ms=ea.65fb9cc2-7296-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjY1ZmI5Y2MyLTcyOTYtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMGQzYTExZmEzMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=r447Nut0YyQ6__9OMHJi6Tsduq_NaEQiH9PextZkP7I=) I have some incredible news out of Minnesota: **Our JanePAC-endorsed climate champion, Peggy Flanagan, won her primary for U.S. Senate last night. 🎉** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137109985/639673168/2105508926?refcode=ea.65fb9cc2-7296-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ms=ea.65fb9cc2-7296-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjY1ZmI5Y2MyLTcyOTYtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMGQzYTExZmEzMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=r447Nut0YyQ6__9OMHJi6Tsduq_NaEQiH9PextZkP7I=) Peggy was up against more than **$10 million in outside spending** — dark money super PACs, special interests like Chevron, and yes, even AI-generated deepfakes designed to make voters believe she'd taken the very corporate money she's spent her career refusing. It was an ugly fight. It was well-funded. _But it didn't work._ This primary was a litmus test for what voters actually want from the Democratic Party. **Given a choice between a candidate beholden to billionaires and corporate super PACs and a candidate who built a people-powered movement from the ground up, Minnesotans chose people power.** That sends a message far beyond Minnesota's borders. Every dollar, every door knocked, every conversation had — it all added up to something Big Oil and dark money couldn't buy their way past. And Peggy wasn't the only win for our movement in Minnesota last night. JanePAC-endorsed Attorney General Keith Ellison secured his primary victory too, keeping a proven climate and consumer champion on track to continue holding polluters accountable from one of the most powerful legal offices in the state. **These results fill me with hope, and I’m immensely grateful for your continued support. And Peggy wasn't the only win for our movement in Minnesota last night. JanePAC-endorsed Attorney General Keith Ellison secured his primary victory too, keeping a proven climate and consumer champion on track to continue holding polluters accountable from one of the most powerful legal offices in the state. The U.S. government has **[sold a Venezuela-linked oil tanker seized after a dramatic high-seas chase,](https://substack.com/redirect/4bc5d784-48f8-4056-b54c-c47e72064185?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** clearing the way for the dark-fleet vessel to be demolished by its new owner.

---|---|---
* **Chase spanned the Atlantic:** The sanctioned Bella 1 fled a Caribbean blockade, changed names, and painted a Russian flag before its capture off Iceland.
* **Captain sentenced last week:** A U.S. district court sentenced the ship's captain for refusing Coast Guard orders during the weeks-long pursuit.
* **Treasury licenses enabled sale:** Vessel-specific licenses allowed Global Marketing Systems to buy the tanker without dealing with sanctioned owners.
* **Recycling aims to block return:** Officials and the buyer said demolition prevents the vessel from re-entering illicit trade and removes environmental risk.

# [Meta and Nvidia just seized the open-weight AI crown](https://substack.com/redirect/21978de0-89f1-4824-9434-f0698a02bd08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Meta and Nvidia released open-weight AI models this week, **[joining a U.S. tech push to compete with Chinese labs](https://substack.com/redirect/e7a06c5a-e4b7-4629-baa1-d91840e33d42?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while urging policymakers against premature restrictions on the technology.

---|---|---
* **Meta opens Muse Glimmer:** Meta released Muse Glimmer on Monday and plans to open the weights of its more powerful Muse Spark 1.2 model for free developer access.
* **Nvidia debuts Nemotron Lightning:** Nvidia followed with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, publishing training datasets, techniques, and model weights as truly open-source offerings.
* **Tech letter defends openness:** More than 20 U.S. companies recently urged officials to avoid premature restrictions on open-weight models, including those developed in China.
* **Domestic models gain appeal:** Box CEO Aaron Levie said the releases plant a firm flag that America will field near-frontier open-source models suitable for sensitive users.

* **Targets include spas and pharmacies:** The suits name compounding pharmacies, medical spas, and online sellers that marketed Retatrutide products to consumers.
* **FDA already banned unapproved sales:** In June the FDA stated that sales of Retatrutide and other unapproved GLP-1 versions to consumers are illegal.
* **More than 200 referrals made:** Lilly has referred over 200 individuals and entities to the FDA, Justice Department, and state authorities.
* **Customs seizures surge sharply:** U.S. Customs intercepted more than 1,400 shipments and nearly 90,000 vials of illicit GLP-1 drugs in July alone.

* * *
* * *
# [China's Boeing rival C919 makes historic first international flight](https://substack.com/redirect/21978de0-89f1-4824-9434-f0698a02bd08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
China's COMAC C919 completed its first scheduled international commercial flight Wednesday, flying from Beijing to Ulaanbaatar as the state-owned maker **[seeks to challenge the Boeing-Airbus duopoly.](https://substack.com/redirect/8a2e7822-5ca9-4ff5-b90a-23a60bbbf9a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/21978de0-89f1-4824-9434-f0698a02bd08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Daily Beijing-Ulaanbaatar service begins:** Air China will operate the narrow-body jet on the route every day after the inaugural departure just after 3 p.m. local time.
* **Foreign parts still limit reach:** The aircraft relies on foreign components and lacks U.S. or European certification, restricting sales outside China.
* **Delivery pace lags far behind targets:** COMAC delivered only 15 C919s last year against a goal of 75, well below Boeing and Airbus output.
* **Analysts question competitive speed:** Experts say production remains too slow and in-service support must still match established rivals for real impact.

* * *
* * *
# [Mortgage rates finally dip and applications jump back to life](https://substack.com/redirect/21978de0-89f1-4824-9434-f0698a02bd08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
After five weeks of increases, the average 30-year fixed **[mortgage rate edged down to 6.77% last week,](https://substack.com/redirect/74a8e512-401e-4e44-9cd0-6390dead8e69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** prompting a 3.6% rise in total mortgage application volume.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/21978de0-89f1-4824-9434-f0698a02bd08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Refinance applications climb 5%:** Refinance volume rose for the week yet remained 22% below the same period a year earlier when rates were lower.
* **Purchase applications also improve:** Applications to buy homes increased 3% week-over-week but stayed 1% lower than the year-ago level.
* **August remains seasonally weak:** High home prices and economic uncertainty continue to weigh on what is typically one of the slowest sales months.
* **CPI report looms over rates:** Market participants are watching Wednesday's consumer price index for potential larger moves in borrowing costs.

Fellow Patriot, Tyler's message absolutely broke my heart, and I'd like you to read it if you have a moment:
My name is Tyler Tew. I was a commercial airline pilot for 14 years. I flew for SkyWest as a Captain and then Allegiant. I graduated from Utah State with an aviation degree and built my entire life around flying. I went to Washington on January 6 after being invited by friends.

After President Trump's speech, I went to the Capitol. What I saw with my own eyes did not match what the news reported.

On March 26, 2021, **the TSA revoked my commercial pilot 's license for "suspicion of terrorism"** and being a threat to the national airspace -- before I was ever charged with a crime and before any FBI interview.**I spent $40,000 in legal fees. **

In June 2021, Allegiant fired me. Without my W-2 income, I could no longer sustain the construction company my wife and I owned. It is now in bankruptcy. We have four children. I now work 6-7 days a week in construction just to survive.

| | Every day, families in El Paso are forced to make difficult decisions about keeping the lights on, keeping food on the table, or cooling their homes — all thanks to rising utility costs and extreme temperatures. **This is a choice no one should have to make. That's exactly why I'm renewing my call for Congress to act by advancing my legislative package to lower energy costs for families by accelerating access to reliable, affordable clean energy.** It's long overdue for the Republican-held Congress to deliver meaningful energy relief instead of protecting the ballooning profits of energy companies. Here's how my legislative package increases accountability and drastically expands assistance for families struggling with utility costs:
* The**Lowering Utility Bills Act** : Establishes much stronger federal and state standards for how electricity providers calculate their rates. By strengthening oversight, customers won't be forced to pay out-of-control rates that line the pockets of utility companies.
* The**Heating and Cooling Relief Act** : Helps low-income households afford heating and cooling costs by expanding and modernizing the _Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program_.
* The**Energy Bills Relief Act** : Reinstates the 2022 clean energy tax credits for home energy improvements that Trump cut. This act prioritizes working families by driving down energy costs amid President Trump's war of choice with Iran, which is causing global energy market volatility.

clean_body: | | | | Every day, families in El Paso are forced to make difficult decisions about keeping the lights on, keeping food on the table, or cooling their homes — all thanks to rising utility costs and extreme temperatures. This is a choice no one should have to make. That's exactly why I'm renewing my call for Congress to act by advancing my legislative package to lower energy costs for families by accelerating access to reliable, affordable clean energy. It's long overdue for the Republican-held Congress to deliver meaningful energy relief instead of protecting the ballooning profits of energy companies. Here's how my legislative package increases accountability and drastically expands assistance for families struggling with utility costs: TheLowering Utility Bills Act : Establishes much stronger federal and state standards for how electricity providers calculate their rates. By strengthening oversight, customers won't be forced to pay out-of-control rates that line the pockets of utility companies. TheHeating and Cooling Relief Act : Helps low-income households afford heating and cooling costs by expanding and modernizing the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program. TheEnergy Bills Relief Act : Reinstates the 2022 clean energy tax credits for home energy improvements that Trump cut. This act prioritizes working families by driving down energy costs amid President Trump's war of choice with Iran, which is causing global energy market volatility. Texas-16 needs a representative with common sense and grit to hold companies profiting off of our suffering accountable.= No matter the cost, I will keep fighting for you. | | **No False Promises**
---
| | **Dear Alaskans,** In one week on Tuesday, August 18, you'll decide who moves on to the November election. In a crowded race like this one, a handful of votes, even two or three, could make all the difference.
We're asking you to vote for **Walker Hoffbeck**.
There are times for learning on the job. And there are times when Alaska needs leaders who already know the job. That time is now.
Bill Walker and Randy Hoffbeck are Independents, just like two-thirds of Alaska. Together they bring decades of experience solving Alaska's toughest challenges. With an energy crisis, a fiscal crisis, and struggling fisheries, Alaska doesn't have time for a learning curve.
You deserve leaders who will tell you the truth. Anyone can promise a full Permanent Fund Dividend. But Alaska's oil production tax revenue has fallen from nearly **$6 billion** a year to about **$600 million**. Without replacing that revenue, those promises simply don't add up.
Instead, Walker Hoffbeck has proposed a **True Resource Dividend** with an annual guarantee of $1,000 that grows as Alaska develops more of its oil, gas, mining, and other natural resources. It's an honest plan built on growing Alaska's economy, not making promises that can't be kept.
Alaska's open primary gives every voter the same voice. The top four candidates move on, regardless of party. When independent leadership succeeds, **all Alaskans win.** It means solutions come before ideology and Alaska comes before politics.
**If you want your voice to be heard, you have to vote. Early voting is underway. Find out where you can vote today:**[ https://www.elections.alaska.gov/voter-information/absentee-and-early-voting/](https://us.list-manage.com/xMeFusiRM8Y?e=b6cf32d1c2&c2id=bccaf449ed2960725e09a7036fc7e612)
**Please vote by August 18.****Vote Walker Hoffbeck.****No false promises. Just honest solutions.**

**Bill Walker** \- Candidate for Governor**Randy Hoffbeck** \- Candidate for Lieutenant Governor
**Learn more about us and our bluebrint for a robust Alaska at:**[**www.walkerhoffbeck.com**](https://us.list-manage.com/39Sh_7jHBjC?e=b6cf32d1c2&c2id=bccaf449ed2960725e09a7036fc7e612)
P.S. Every contribution, [whether it’s $26, $50, $100, or any amount you choose](https://us.list-manage.com/12dzDg_MIXm?e=b6cf32d1c2&c2id=bccaf449ed2960725e09a7036fc7e612), helps us build the campaign Alaska deserves. Thank you for standing with us.

| Some folks around here still say a Black man can't win a statewide election in Louisiana. I hear it all the time.
We haven't had a black US Senator or statewide elected official since Reconstruction. But I'm a farmer. And I know what grows in this soil.
My family worked this Delta land when they were slaves and then sharecroppers. Today my son and I farm the very same fields together - but now we own it. So don't tell me what's "impossible" in Louisiana.

Dear Peter, The Trump administration is once again putting Oregon’s public forests on the chopping block. The U.S. Forest Service has released a draft plan that could **triple logging across 5.5 million acres of eastern Oregon’s national forests** over the next decade—including the Malheur, Ochoco, Umatilla, and Wallowa-Whitman National Forests. **Will you make an urgent donation today to help OLCV fight back and protect Oregon’s public forests?**
---
[ **Donate to Defend Oregon’s Forests** ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137118864/639694774/1784380013?amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkxDVi8xLzcwODc3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjE1ZWEyZDczLTgwOTYtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMGQzYTExZmEzMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=_M8I4jieNPZAr2m4mg3KkTHXYjqIWSWEAIXphZUvmME=&emci=d523766b-7596-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=15ea2d73-8096-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=2107230)
---
Your support today gives OLCV the resources to respond when Oregon’s public lands are threatened—from mobilizing thousands of Oregonians to speak up, to advocating for science-based forest management, and holding decision-makers accountable. There's a lot at stake right now. This proposal would weaken long-standing protections for large, mature trees and assumes the elimination of safeguards that have protected millions of acres of roadless forests. The Forest Service claims dramatically increasing logging will reduce wildfire risk, against the concerns of many scientists and conservation advocates. These forests are some of Oregon’s greatest natural treasures. They provide clean drinking water; store climate-polluting carbon; support wildlife like wolves, salmon, elk, and owls; and offer places for people to hike, hunt, fish, and recreate. **Your donation today will help OLCV continue fighting for our forests, clean water, wildlife, and climate resilience.**
---

---
Our public forests belong to all of us. Thank you for standing with OLCV and helping protect Oregon for generations to come. With sincere gratitude,

clean_body: Will you make an urgent donation today to help OLCV fight back and protect Oregon’s public forests?| | | Dear Peter, The Trump administration is once again putting Oregon’s public forests on the chopping block. The U.S. Forest Service has released a draft plan that could triple logging across 5.5 million acres of eastern Oregon’s national forests over the next decade—including the Malheur, Ochoco, Umatilla, and Wallowa-Whitman National Forests. Will you make an urgent donation today to help OLCV fight back and protect Oregon’s public forests? Your support today gives OLCV the resources to respond when Oregon’s public lands are threatened—from mobilizing thousands of Oregonians to speak up, to advocating for science-based forest management, and holding decision-makers accountable. There's a lot at stake right now. This proposal would weaken long-standing protections for large, mature trees and assumes the elimination of safeguards that have protected millions of acres of roadless forests. The Forest Service claims dramatically increasing logging will reduce wildfire risk, against the concerns of many scientists and conservation advocates. These forests are some of Oregon’s greatest natural treasures. They provide clean drinking water; store climate-polluting carbon; support wildlife like wolves, salmon, elk, and owls; and offer places for people to hike, hunt, fish, and recreate. Your donation today will help OLCV continue fighting for our forests, clean water, wildlife, and climate resilience. Our public forests belong to all of us. Thank you for standing with OLCV and helping protect Oregon for generations to come. With sincere gratitude, April Christenson (she/her) OLCV Development Director P.S. — Oregon’s public forests need champions who will stand up for them. Your donation today helps OLCV mobilize members like you to fight back. Thanks for all you do. | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Oregon League of Conservation Voters 1110 SE Alder Suite 220 Portland, OR 97214 United States If you believe you received this message in error or wish to no longer receive email from us, please .

Denver ballot measure would drop citizenship rule for police-fire oversight board
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hey friends,
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** Complete Colorado warns Initiative 195's progressive-tax pitch echoes 1913's income-tax promises, [raising bracket-creep concerns](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Douglas County is set to approve a [$19.3M tax rebate for a new Flexential data center](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as Front Range cities restrict the industry. Denver Mayor Johnston [filed for reelection](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), citing housing and utility costs. And Denver Council passed 12-0 a charter measure [dropping the citizenship requirement for police/fire oversight commissioners](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), which sponsors call "equity."
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** Newly released texts show Fauci told CDC's Walensky and Dr. Murthy in Jan. 2021 that post-vaccine symptoms ["theoretically could be associated with miscarriage in the 1st trimester"](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.); Sens. Johnson and Paul released the messages, citing informed consent.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** The Gazette notes a funding bill [delays the federal hemp crackdown a month](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), with Bennet and Hickenlooper backing it. Hillman cites Kiros' win over DeGette and Rutinel's CD8 win as a [DSA wave in Colorado](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Joondeph notes Flo-Jo's records are regularly beaten by high schoolers, backing the [IOC's biological eligibility standard](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). And James reports Manitou Springs funded extra Rangers to [keep the coffin races](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) on for Oct. 24.
This is your Mountain Minute for Wednesday, August 12, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Denver ballot measure would drop citizenship rule for police-fire oversight board](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
This November, Denver voters will decide whether to change the city charter with a ballot question that never mentions the word “citizenship.”
The question they’ll see asks whether the charter should be “amended to modernize the Civil Service Commission and Department of Safety by removing outdated language, giving City Council the ability to add duties via code, and providing for an extension of probation when required for medical, military, or other approved leave.”
Nothing in that sentence tells a voter that one of the things being removed is the requirement that the people who oversee the hiring of every Denver police officer and firefighter be United States citizens. But that is what the measure does.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Colorado Progressive Tax Plan Raises Long-Term Bracket Creep Concerns](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COMPLETE COLORADO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_Behind the promise that 97% of filers get a tax cut lies an unindexed bracket system that could quietly raise taxes on everyone over time._
* **A familiar promise from history:** Nash Herman draws a parallel to the 1913 federal income tax, which was sold as affecting only about 1% of the population before eventually reaching nearly everyone — arguing Initiative 195's claim that 97% of filers get a cut suffers from the same static, short-sighted framing.
* **Unindexed brackets mean rising real tax burdens:** Initiative 195's six new tax brackets aren't adjusted for inflation, so as wages rise — partly from inflation alone — filers get pushed into higher brackets even as their actual purchasing power stays flat or falls behind.
* **The math plays out fast:** A filer at Colorado's average taxable income of $81,800 would cross into a higher bracket within five years under historical inflation and wage-growth trends — reaching that bracket in just five years instead of the twelve it would take if brackets were inflation-indexed, despite having the purchasing power of only about $89,000 at that point.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

Neither utility was legally required to join. Both chose to._
____

**BY SHAINA COLE | LOCAL | AUGUST 5** _The chief security officer of the Denver Security Office sent a resignation email to more than a dozen recipients at 12:57 p.m. on July 2 — the day after his seven-year anniversary with the city — and used the letter to accuse General Services leaders of punishing him for raising concerns._
**[A union pipeline DSA built on college campuses](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | AUGUST 4**
_DSA’s youth section trains students to organize on campus. What happens after graduation is its own story, one its own members describe directly. “YDSA’s job is to train socialists on campus and create a pipeline into DSA,” Dare Cima, a University of Louisville YDSA member, said at the organization’s national conference this spring._**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**__

And for 30 years, Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. And I’m sick of it.

My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation logger.

**[This weekend, I officially earned the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate. Now it’s time to defeat Susan Collins and her billionaire backers. Let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me.

When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.

After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change unless there were working-class voices in power.

So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.

I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.

body:
$1B for Trump’s ego, $0 for working families.
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137120135/639698960/623074613?refcode=jtk1473-fr-nd1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3OTQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDYyOWM0MzgtODQ5Ni1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=gAC7pnX2iYxgVj6Ij4vUzraQCuCRfDiulOw_nBnSaHs=&emci=7018b99a-0595-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=4629c438-8496-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=9329426)
---
Friend, right now, everyday Americans across Connecticut and the country are struggling to make ends meet. Families are trying to put food on the table, keep up with soaring housing costs, and pay for basic healthcare.
**Yet while you work hard to stretch every dollar, Donald Trump is treating our nation’s capital like his personal Versailles — spending upwards of $1 billion on 18 vanity projects.**
He demolished the historic East Wing of the White House to build a lavish ballroom, repainted and ruined the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool (which now sits empty and fenced off), and is planning a massive triumphal arch to glorify himself.
The price tags are eye-popping, and the quality is abysmal:
* **$600 Million for the White House East Wing:** A project that ballooned from $200 million to $400 million, and now to $600 million, handed out in a single-source, no-bid contract.
* **More Than $16 Million for the Reflecting Pool:** Handed through a noncompetitive contract to a water-filtration company owned by a Trump campaign donor who has given over $300,000. The work was so poorly done that it has to be completely reworked — likely doubling the cost.
* **$17 Million More for Lafayette Park:** A project originally budgeted at $3.3 million that jumped to $17 million under another no-bid contract.

This isn’t just reckless waste. It’s blatant corruption.
Think about where that $1 billion could have gone instead. That money could be lowering healthcare costs by extending ACA subsidies, securing food assistance through SNAP, investing in public education, or providing affordable housing to families in desperate need.
Instead, Trump consistently refuses to help the American people with the struggles they face. These aren’t the actions of a leader serving the public; they are the hallmarks of someone only concerned with himself and enriching his political allies.
**Trump would rather pay upwards of a billion dollars for self-aggrandizing vanity projects than spend a dime to help the American people with very common struggles._[Please join me in our fight against a president who could not care less about the people he is supposed to serve.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137120136/639698961/-1263650200?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1473-fr-nd1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3OTQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDYyOWM0MzgtODQ5Ni1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=gAC7pnX2iYxgVj6Ij4vUzraQCuCRfDiulOw_nBnSaHs=)_**

Friend,
Most gun owners NEVER see this part of the fight.
No courtroom. No cameras. Just a _**federal comment docket**_ , a hard deadline, and a stack of proposed rules that will govern how you buy, keep, and travel with your firearms for _years to come._
The ATF put **34 proposed and final rules** on the table this spring. Our Executive Director, Adam Kraut, was in the room when they were announced. The anti-gun lobby has been ___in an uproar_ _ever since._
**So we filed.**
Here is exactly what the Second Amendment Foundation formally asked the ATF to do:
1. Clear out the _**outdated barriers**_ to firearms transactions that do not happen face-to-face at a dealer's counter.
2. Put a reasonable limit back on how long dealers are _**forced to hold records**_ with _your name_ on them.
3. Strengthen _**protections for interstate travel**_ with _your firearms_ under the Gun Control Act and the Firearm Owners' Protection Act.
4. Cut the red tape that _**punishes lawfully owned NFA items**_ the moment they cross a state line.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137120304/639699469/-785282667?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZTg4ODllMS04NDk2LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3OzRYp5vlbjW7h5kNaAmIr1lKLNnJtyqT4R7_YDo6ek=)

Peter, I woke up today feeling incredibly grateful. _**Thank you, Vermont.**_ Thank you to everyone who cast a ballot yesterday. Thank you to the election workers who make our democracy possible. Thank you to the volunteers, supporters, neighbors, and community members who keep showing up because you believe our government can be led with courage, kindness, and care for one another. And thank you for continuing to trust me to represent this extraordinary state in Congress. **I never, ever take that responsibility for granted.** One of the things I love most about Vermont is that we understand democracy is something _we do together._ It happens when we vote. It happens when someone steps forward and puts their name on a ballot. It happens at town meeting, around kitchen tables, at community events, and in conversations between neighbors who may not agree on everything but still care deeply about this beautiful place we call home. I am also grateful to every Vermonter who was willing to step forward and run for office this year. Putting yourself out there and asking your neighbors for their trust takes courage, and our democracy is stronger when more people are willing to serve. **Now, the primary is behind us, and there is plenty of work ahead.** Families across Vermont are still feeling squeezed by the cost of housing, healthcare, groceries, and everyday life. Vermonters are worried about Social Security and Medicare, about their rights and freedoms, and about whether Washington is actually listening to the people it is supposed to serve. **Those are the things I am thinking about today. Those are the people I am thinking about today. And that is the work I am heading back to.** You know me. I’m going to keep fighting to lower costs, protect the programs Vermonters depend on, defend our freedoms, and make sure Vermont’s voice is heard loud and clear in DC. **But today, more than anything, I just wanted to say thank you.** Serving you is the honor of my life. With enormous gratitude, — Becca

body:
| | | | | [|

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Friends,The dust has settled from the primary, and I feel very good about where we finished. Mike Kelly seems convinced this race is over. He has characterized his primary victory as a referendum on the status quo, proof, in his view, that Johnson County voters want more of the same.My response?**Hold my beer. I’m just getting started.** Go ahead and underestimate me. I’ve been underestimated before.What Mike Kelly doesn’t understand is that this campaign was never about insiders, consultants, or protecting the status quo. It is about the people I meet every single day who are frustrated with rising property taxes, unchecked spending, and a county government that too often seems more interested in defending its decisions than listening to the people paying the bills.And over the next 83 days, we are going to make sure those voices are heard.I know this race will be difficult.**But difficult and impossible are two very different things.** And this is where I need your help.**We need the resources to get our message out.** Mike Kelly has a financial advantage, but he pays his political consultant $12,500 every month (this is CRAZY). I don't need to spend like Mike Kelly to win this race.But I do need your help.Every $25, $50, $100, or $250 contribution helps us reach another voter, put another sign in the ground, send another piece of mail, and make the case for a different direction in Johnson County.[**DONATE HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/ZT34B5sYHo6?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494) And money alone will not win this election.We need people.We are building an army of supporters who believe Johnson County deserves transparent leadership, fiscal sanity, accountability, and a government that remembers whose money it is spending.Knock doors. Make calls. Host a gathering. Put up a sign. Talk to your neighbors.[**JOIN THE TEAM**](https://us.list-manage.com/Hbds9jR5eEo?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494) There comes a point when waiting becomes a choice.We can accept four more years of the status quo and watch our property taxes continue to skyrocket. _Or we can choose a different direction._ I am ready to bring fiscal discipline, transparency, and accountability to Johnson County government.**Enough waiting. It’s time to change course.** I’d be honored to have you standing with me.Karen

Join us as we interview Ivory Hecker a former mainstream television reporter who chose independence over compliance. After stepping away from corporate media, she built her own platform rooted in transparency, integrity, and direct audience connection. Today, her work spans journalism education, holistic wellness exploration, and mission-driven fashion--each expression grounded in the same principle: live and speak truthfully, without compromise.
As a TV reporter Ivory was an anchor for Fox and NBC stations, she had what many would call a dream job. But important stories were watered down or buried -- not because they weren't true, but because they risked upsetting advertisers or rocking the boat. The final straw came during the pandemic. Ivory tried to report a major story that would've helped people make informed health decisions -- but her bosses silenced her and threatened my job.
Live on air, Ivory went off-script. She told the truth -- about the censorship, the corporate control, and the lies. She dared them to fire her. And they did. "It was terrifying. It was exhilarating. And it was the best decision I've ever made." Stated Ivory. In the three years since, leaving that job she has built a six-figure platform, reached hundreds of thousands across social media, and made a bigger impact than she ever could in corporate news. She tried to kill off the Salt River wild horses, a piece of Arizona's identity she'd rather erase than protect. She vetoed No Tax on Tips three separate times before we forced her hand and made her sign it. That's the pattern. Block first. Cave only when the pressure gets too heavy to ignore. Now it 's our turn to apply the pressure that removes her from office entirely. Here's what most people don't realize about this race. It's not just about who sits in the Governor's office in Phoenix. What happens next in Arizona determines what happens in America. Losing Arizona means statistically losing the next presidential race... Which means losing the census fight against the Democratic Socialist of America in 2030... Which means losing the country for the next 20-30 years, possibly for good. The talking heads on cable news want you focused on this week's headlines and next month's jobs report. ### **New Hampshire Republican State Committee Praises Karoline Leavitt’s Service as White House Press Secretary**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** August 12th, 2026
---
| | | **CONTACT** karina@nhrsc.com

---
| |

**CONCORD, N.H. —** The New Hampshire Republican State Committee today praised Karoline Leavitt for her outstanding service as White House Press Secretary following the announcement that she will step down from the position at the end of August to spend more time with her family.A proud Granite Stater, Leavitt has made history as the youngest person ever to serve as White House Press Secretary. Since taking the podium in January 2025, she has represented the Trump Administration with confidence, clarity, and conviction while taking on one of the most demanding and high-profile communications roles in American government.“Karoline Leavitt has made New Hampshire proud,” said **NHRSC Chairman Scott Maltzie**. “From the Granite State to the White House podium, Karoline has shown what can happen when talented, hardworking young Granite Staters step up to serve. She has represented President Trump and his agenda with strength, intelligence, and determination, and she has never backed down from tough questions.”“Karoline has been an exceptional press secretary and a tremendous ambassador for New Hampshire,” Maltzie continued. “We are grateful for her service and for the way she has carried the Granite State with her every step of the way. We wish her nothing but the very best in this next chapter.”Leavitt’s departure marks the conclusion of a historic tenure at the White House, where she served as the sole press secretary of President Donald Trump’s second administration.The New Hampshire Republican State Committee congratulates Karoline on an extraordinary accomplishment. The Granite State will continue to be proud to call her one of its own.

Trump attacked mail-in voting by forcing his cronies installed at the United States Postal Service (USPS) to refuse to deliver ballots to or from voters in states that did not hand over to his Administration sensitive information about voters. Trump wants to gain possession of states' voter rolls so he and his allies can build a federal, MAGA-controlled database of citizens complete with profiles of party registration, models of how people vote and who they support, and identifying info like addresses and Social Security numbers -- so they know exactly who to target when they seize ballots after the November midterm elections. But a judge just put a nationwide freeze on this illicit scheme. Trump will almost certainly ask the MAGA majority on the U.S. Supreme Court to overturn the ruling with less than three months until Election Day. | == Judges see through Trump's bullshit and they are not backing down -- even after Trump and his MAGA horde have leveled threats of violence and even death at those who rule against him. # [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41539%2E3422442%2E3bTBeR)
[](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260812_1_ak.42IWI5&refcode=em20260812-41539_partner_ms_aes_em_truthtopower&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=41539%2E3422442%2E3bTBeR)
Peter, it's Dr. Abdul El-Sayed. I am so proud to be the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan. And now, our general election campaign officially begins.
Sixteen months ago, this campaign launched with a handful of us in a room and one belief: it shouldn't be this hard, in the richest country in the world, to see a doctor, pay your bills, or know your kids will have it better than you did.
**We carried that to every corner of the state. Now there's one job left: beat MAGA Mike Rogers and win a seat that could decide our Senate majority.**
Rogers got a head start. While we fought through an expensive primary, he ran unopposed, with Trump's backing and $45 million in spending building him up. And still, the race is tied. A recent poll has it locked at 45% to 45%.
**This seat is there for us to take. The only question is whether we reach voters before their money does.**
**[Will you split one of the very first donations of our general election between our campaign and Truth to Power? A dollar right now buys the ads that define these races. A dollar in October only answers their attacks. There is no better time to invest than the start.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260812_1_ak.42IWI5&refcode=em20260812-41539_partner_ms_aes_em_truthtopower&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41539%2E3422442%2E3bTBeR)**
[Donate ›››](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260812_1_ak.42IWI5&refcode=em20260812-41539_partner_ms_aes_em_truthtopower&t=4&akid=41539%2E3422442%2E3bTBeR)
And Peter, here's the contrast in this race.
I'm a doctor. Mike Rogers is the guy who introduced the bill that helped Big Pharma flood this country with opioids. More than 600,000 Americans died. He never apologized. Then he took $400,000 from the drug companies that profited.
As Detroit's health director, I spearheaded a program that will cancel up to $700 million in medical debt for 300,000 Michiganders. Rogers spent 30 years in Washington, left up to $14 million richer working for the same corporations he used to regulate.
I trust women to make their own decisions. Rogers voted for a national abortion ban, including one with no exceptions for rape or incest.
**A doctor who answers to Michiganders, or a career politician who has already shown you who he answers to. That's the choice in November.**
Every day we spend playing catch-up is a day their money defines these races before voters hear from us.
**[Split $5 or whatever you can between our campaign and Truth to Power to power us from the very beginning of this general election.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260812_1_ak.42IWI5&refcode=em20260812-41539_partner_ms_aes_em_truthtopower&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=41539%2E3422442%2E3bTBeR)**
[Donate ›››](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260812_1_ak.42IWI5&refcode=em20260812-41539&t=24&akid=41539%2E3422442%2E3bTBeR)
I'd be glad to have you with us from the start.
Thank you so much,
Abdul

clean_body: | | | Peter, It’s only been a week since Abdul El-Sayed won his primary for the U.S. Senate in Michigan, and the political establishment is already conspiring to take him down. According to The New York Times , after spending $32 million for Haley Stevens (and failing), AIPAC is willing to put “tens of millions of dollars” behind Mike Rogers, the Republican incumbent. 1 These are the kinds of sore losers that our WFP champions are up against, Peter. They are so desperate to squash our working class movement that they’d be willing to bankroll election deniers, warmongers, Trump bootlickers, and those responsible for throwing millions off their health care. This is a defining moment for our movement. In primary after primary, we have proven that working people are able to build the kind of political power necessary to change this country. But the ultimate test is in November. We’ll be up against the unified strength of the billionaire class. Republicans and even some Democratic donors, like the ones who fund AIPAC, will stop at nothing to keep our WFP champions out of office. They know that our candidates can’t be bought. And they know that our candidates will actually fight for working families in Congress, rather than just paying them lip service. But we’ve been defeating the billionaire class all year long, having won EIGHTEEN Congressional primaries so far. And we can do the same between now and November. But we need a lot of resources in order to organize, knock on doors, and make calls for them. In solidarity, Team WFP Sources: 1\. , New York Times , August 5, 2026 Thoughts? Feedback? Horrible Katie Hobbs has not debated a single opponent since 2018.

That's the pattern. Block first. Cave only when the pressure gets too heavy to ignore.

**Now it 's our turn to apply the pressure that removes her from office entirely.**

[Defeat Katie Hobbs](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=09d0325884fb456f9890264d27370d6e&_e=4bUUEDjipD0FNl7c-ZvlxoUyctiSWCPbZverBbWsxtSM6sTL85PZuymoZln2Z8WTQGpaW01hfnGfneJD4mspkbL4dK5BOpSb4oFtPqtT7_rWs4CdQE8LFYhEno0dpwAnsT415a4ABAf52QLf_aPUUsQIOn-h1TlnDehrSyj5pkn1ainqZzBvTlSUpDM1pBYSZoBcKartyRWy5tqpu87Y5TQDHBlM187sGJhoGNAM4GTnI1bY0y6xsxZtpRSA8zUC7sUgpuORCHmVjPhBDHgTENRD-f6MGK9Ag5JPHVB7GPJcZSfXMSatUJ0aTbvS_e4hz9u5vro2XXQ7D3NgZ3aAZPDJFYOsA-Q2W_rfO_x9Pr5og2kDxP_aUUGf1pfYBRXWR7bxLrfZFwr4OMPqdCFtZjnU2RrYM0IdsO_l484khlivR3F8k3AzvNs4Me_lS8NfmV5lde04PRq6Vbnwf_lTamXlugO_pYsiVyCRHnOcJwSrjAILpG4kTMjs0v1bud2OZOP3sG0W6kb1dBnw0d1VjyO_7ao6jEZAB5iJsrBQum2iP-MZ1R3QpFQRgeUDAMG2GwY4O0dQc8hApexOgP3klUbdxf4Ej_nmQk9cBdimCQlWsOrz53s9uK9o4JDJ6oZcPxbSSi0PtY_mwhOPGeaPAmjy2qya4PEWsDGLSwzTqDw%3D)

Here's what most people don't realize about this race. It's not just about who sits in the Governor's office in Phoenix.

**What happens next in Arizona determines what happens in America. **

Losing Arizona means statistically losing the next presidential race...

Which means losing the census fight against the Democratic Socialist of America in 2030...

Which means losing the country for the next 20-30 years, possibly for good.

The talking heads on cable news want you focused on this week's headlines and next month's jobs report. That's not where this election gets decided.

**This election, and our future, will be decided by who 's knocking doors and chasing ballots in the next 90 days.**

| | We launched our campaign for Congress with a belief that our community deserves better and a scrappiness that’s unique to Michigan’s 10th. I knew this journey would require sacrifice, and I also knew it would come with incredible moments. I want to share my favorite part of this experience with you:
---
It’s the conversations that stay with you.
Sometimes those conversations are hard. Seniors worried about rising grocery costs and threats to Social Security. Working parents doing everything they can to stay afloat while giving their kids the best life possible. A neighbor quietly sharing concerns about her mother’s recent cancer diagnosis.
Sometimes those conversations are full of joy: “I’ve never actually had a politician knock on my door before!” “My daughter is starting at Michigan in the fall!” “DEEETROIT BASKETBALL!”
These moments are my favorite part of this race because they remind me why this campaign matters. At the end of the day, people want to know that someone in Washington is listening and willing to fight for them. These conversations also remind me that even in difficult times, we can still build something better together for our families, our communities, and our future.

name: Peggy Flanagan (via DNC HQ)
subject: In almost 250 years, there’s never been a Native woman serving in the US Senate.
body:
---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-flanagan-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260812_8568_fr&refcode2=8568_22930333_IIvw5S&akid=8568%2E22930333%2EIIvw5S)
---
Derek, in almost 250 years, there’s never been a Native woman serving in the US Senate. **It’s time to change that.**
I’m Peggy Flanagan, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota.
I am Ojibwe and a proud member of the White Earth Nation. My family is the Wolf Clan. The mission of my clan is to never leave anyone behind — and that’s been my guiding principle.
I am the descendant of people who were forced off their land onto the White Earth reservation. I am the relative of residential boarding school survivors. I am the daughter of a man who always spoke truth to power for the good of the Anishinaabe people.
I’m thinking of my daughter — who just got her first jingle dress — and whether or not she will see Indigenous women in all parts of our government.
**Right now, there are no Native voices in the US Senate._If I win this race, we can change that._**
[**It's high time that all our communities have a seat at the table. If you agree, will you pitch in $20 or whatever you can to power my campaign and the DNC and help me make history?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-flanagan-split?refcode=em_20260812_8568_fr&amount=20&refcode2=8568_22930333_IIvw5S&akid=8568%2E22930333%2EIIvw5S)
**[DONATE](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-flanagan-split?refcode=em_20260812_8568_fr&amount=20&refcode2=8568_22930333_IIvw5S&akid=8568%2E22930333%2EIIvw5S)**
Too often, Native voices are ignored or erased in the halls of power.
That’s how we get awful so-called leaders like Donald Trump and J.D. Vance, who called Indigenous Peoples' Day a “fake holiday” and said that Native land was “enemy territory.”
My Ojibwe name means 'Speaks in a Loud and Clear Voice woman.' So I’m using that voice to call out MAGA extremism — loudly and clearly.
But I can’t do it alone. I need your help to build a campaign strong enough to cut through the noise. [**That’s why I’m personally asking, Derek, will you pitch in a split gift between my campaign and the DNC to help us make history and take back the Senate?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-flanagan-split?refcode=em_20260812_8568_fr&amount=20&refcode2=8568_22930333_IIvw5S&akid=8568%2E22930333%2EIIvw5S)
